title: Karim Khan ousted as prosecutor of international criminal court | International criminal court | The Guardian
description: Member states vote to remove British barrister after allegations of sexual abuse
Author: Harry Davies
Headline: Member states vote to remove British barrister after allegations of sexual abuse
Content: Karim Khan has repeatedly denied the allegations.Photograph: Piroschka Van De Wouw/ReutersView image in fullscreenKarim Khan has repeatedly denied the allegations.Photograph: Piroschka Van De Wouw/ReutersInternational criminal courtKarim Khan ousted as prosecutor of international criminal courtMember states vote to remove British barrister after allegations of sexual abuseHarry DaviesFri 24 Jul 2026 14.37 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 18.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe prosecutor of the international criminal court, Karim Khan, has been removed from office after the court’s governing body concluded in June that he had committed serious misconduct in connection to allegations of sexual abuse.The ICC’s member states voted on Friday to oust the British prosecutor in an unprecedented move that concludes a damaging episode for the court two years after the allegations were first raised.According to sources familiar with the result, 82 of the court’s 125 member states voted in favour of removing Khan at a special meeting at the UN’s headquarters in New York.ICC chief prosecutor Karim Khan suspended amid sexual misconduct inquiryRead moreThe vote follows a drawn-outdisciplinary processthat examined the abuse allegations, which were made by a woman who worked for Khan at the ICC.Khan has repeatedly denied all the allegations against him, which include claims that he engaged in coercive and non-consensual sexual behaviour over an extended period.His lawyers have criticised the disciplinary process as procedurally unfair. Responding to the vote, they said Khan would “challenge the lawfulness and fairness of the decision through all available legal mechanisms”.The prominent British barrister was elected in 2021 to serve a nine-year mandate running the court’s prosecution division, which is tasked with investigating and bringing to trial individuals accused of atrocities.During his tenure, Khan’s decisions to obtain arrest warrants for the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, and the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, raised the ICC’s profile and thrust it into the crosshairs of major powers.The warrants, issued by judges, are unaffected by his removal. However, the court’s prosecution division, which has about 400 staff, has been left bruised by a protracted scandal and convoluted process to resolve the matter.Last month, the executive committee of the ICC’s governing bodysuspended Khan after concludinghe had committed serious misconduct in connection to the sexual abuse claims, referring the outcome to member states for a decision on whether to permanently remove him.In a closed-door session on Friday, diplomats voted after reviewing the findings of the executive committee, alongside a fact-finding report by a UN watchdog and a legal analysis of its investigation by a panel of judges.Thirteen member states voted against removing Khan in the secret ballot, while 11 countries abstained.After the allegationsfirst emerged in 2024, Khan’s representatives have sought to suggest the claims may be part of a plot to discredit him in response to his 2024 decision to seek arrest warrants for Netanyahu and his then defence minister.In a report detailing the outcome of the disciplinary process against Khan, the ICC’s governing body found there was no evidence to support claims the woman was “being used by third parties, including intelligence agencies”.Last week, the staffer spoke out against claims she was some sort of “state agent”in an interviewwith CNN’s Christiane Amanpour. She said: “My complaint was because of what happened to me, not for any other reason.”Danya Chaikel, the International Federation for Human Rights’ representative to the ICC, said the vote was a testament to the complainant’s “extraordinary courage in coming forward, despite everything she risked in doing so”.Khan also faced sexual misconduct allegations from a second woman. Shecame forward to the Guardian last yearand accused Khan of mistreating her while she was working for him as an intern earlier in his career.Khan lawyers have previously said he categorically denies having “harassed or mistreated any individual”.In a statement, his lawyer Tayab Ali said: “Khan’s removal was determined by a process in which he was never given a fair opportunity to be heard.” He said the decision was “unsupported by any lawful or properly reasoned finding”.Khan’s dismissal comes as the court faces an array of pressures, includingrenewed threatsfrom the US. The Trump administration has imposed sanctions on several ICC judges and prosecutors andlast week vowedto “systematically disable the ICC’s ability to operate”.Senior officials at the court’s headquarters in The Hague do not expect the US government’s hostility towards the court to diminish with a change in prosecutor.Against this backdrop, the court must now appoint a new prosecutor. After Khan stepped aside last year pending an outcome to the disciplinary process, his two deputies took over the running of the court’s prosecution office.Prosecutors are elected by the ICC’s member states. Some in the prosecution division believe one of the deputies should take over, while others feel it needs a fresh start after two years of turmoil.Explore more on these topicsInternational criminal courtnewsShareReuse this content

title: Five officers injured as police boat strikes Westminster Bridge | London | The Guardian
description: Metropolitan police say officers on marine policing boat are receiving treatment after incident in central London
Author: Hayden Vernon
Headline: Metropolitan police say officers on marine policing boat are receiving treatment after incident in central London
Content: Traffic across Westminster Bridge was brought to a standstill after the incident, with a cordon in place at either end.Photograph: Jaimi Joy/ReutersView image in fullscreenTraffic across Westminster Bridge was brought to a standstill after the incident, with a cordon in place at either end.Photograph: Jaimi Joy/ReutersLondonFive officers injured as police boat strikes Westminster BridgeMetropolitan police say officers on marine policing boat are receiving treatment after incident in central LondonHayden VernonFri 24 Jul 2026 13.29 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 13.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFive officers have been injured after a police boat struck Westminster Bridge in centralLondonon Friday afternoon.TheMetropolitan policesaid the incident occurred at about 3.40pm and involved a boat from the marine policing unit.A spokesperson for the Met said: “A number of officers entered the water but were recovered. Additional officers responded alongside the London ambulance service and London fire brigade.“We understand five officers were injured and are receiving treatment. We await an update on the extent of their injuries. At this stage, we don’t believe any members of the public were involved or injured.“The circumstances of the incident will be thoroughly reviewed, but at this stage our priority is the wellbeing of the officers involved.”Responders from the Royal National Lifeboat Institution could be seen treating casualties on a boat moored at Westminster pier. A large number of police officers, fire crews and ambulances were at the scene, with a police helicopter and air ambulance circling above.Traffic across the bridge was brought to a standstill, with a cordon in place at either end.A mother and son, Cecilia Lusevic, 56, and Mateo Bilis-Lusevic, 12, said they heard a loud bang when the police boat crashed.View image in fullscreenPolice officers, fire crews and ambulances attended the scene, along with a police helicopter and air ambulance.Photograph: Jaimi Joy/ReutersThe visitors to the UK, from Chile, were on a tour boat on the north side of Westminster Bridge and saw what happened, before being evacuated from their boat.Mateo told the Press Association: “Two boats were riding extremely fast through the water. Suddenly, I heard a boom. I was looking towards the boat, and I heard a boom. Then three people went flying into the water, and one of the people was really hurt.”The police officers were in the water for an estimated 10 minutes, he said, and in that time someone threw a life ring in for one of them.In a post on X, the London fire brigade said: “We’re responding to an incident on the #RiverThames near Westminster Bridge alongside partner agencies. The brigade’s fire boat and three fire rescue units with water rescue capabilities have been mobilised to the scene. We were called at 15.58 and remain on scene.“We are supporting the response and providing assistance where needed, working closely with the Metropolitan police, HM Coastguard and partner agencies to manage the situation.”Transport for London said exits one and two at Westminster tube station were closed. Thames Clippers, which operates Uber Boat, said “some services” may be subject to disruption as a result of the incident. It said Westminster pier was closed until further notice.Explore more on these topicsLondonPoliceMetropolitan policeEnglandnewsShareReuse this content

title: Reform councillors told to call donations inquiry ‘establishment stitch-up’ | Reform UK | The Guardian
description: Party briefing notes say: ‘Daily routine of hit jobs and smears will not deter us from winning next general election’
Author: Alexandra Topping
Headline: Party briefing notes say: ‘Daily routine of hit jobs and smears will not deter us from winning next general election’
Content: Police are investigating donations worth £500,000 made to Nigel Farage’s party by the mother the crypto gambler and convicted fraudster George Cottrell.Photograph: Joe Giddens/PAView image in fullscreenPolice are investigating donations worth £500,000 made to Nigel Farage’s party by the mother the crypto gambler and convicted fraudster George Cottrell.Photograph: Joe Giddens/PAReform UKReform councillors told to call donations inquiry ‘establishment stitch-up’Party briefing notes say: ‘Daily routine of hit jobs and smears will not deter us from winning next general election’Alexandra ToppingPolitical correspondentFri 24 Jul 2026 13.12 EDTFirst published on Fri 24 Jul 2026 11.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleReform UK has instructed its councillors to describe a police investigation into donations from the mother of George Cottrell as an establishment stitch-up, as polling showed the party’s popularity plummeting.Internal briefing documents circulated to the party’s councillors included instructions to respond to questions about aMetropolitan police investigationinto party donations with: “It is now clear that the establishment will try anything to stop us”, theTimes revealed on Thursday.Local government representatives were also instructed to respond to questions with: “The British people are tired of the establishment media doing anything they can to stop Reform. A daily routine of hit jobs and smears will not deter us from winning the next general election and fixing broken Britain.”Police areinvestigating donations worth £500,000made to Reform UK by Fiona Cottrell, the mother of the crypto-gambler and convicted fraudster “Posh George”, who is a close friend of Farage.The Guardianrevealed in Aprilthat the Reform UK leader had received a£5m giftfrom the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne before the last election, which iscurrently subject to standards inquiry. The Conservativeshave also asked HMRC to investigatewhether Farage should have paid tax on the £5m gift. Farage is alsosubject to another inquiryover allegations that he breached parliamentary rules by being financially supported by Cottrell.View image in fullscreenGeorge Cottrell beside Farage on the campaign trail in 2024, when the Reform leader was doused in milkshake.Photograph: James Manning/PAHow to Launder Money But Not Like Me, by George Cottrell (as imagined by John Crace)Read moreNew polling by YouGov shows that NigelFarage’s popularity has plummeted, falling to the joint lowest level in the decade it has been tracked by the pollster. Only 22% of people have a positive view of Farage, while 68% see him in a negative light – a net favourability rating of -46.YouGov said the figure was on a par with figures recorded by Boris Johnson after the first “partygate” revelations had broken (-42 in early December 2021) and Keir Starmer just before his resignation (-45).The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, is also enjoying popularity levels higher than those of any Conservative leader for more than five years, according to the survey.Separate polling byMore in Commonindicated that Burnham’s personal approval rating is already higher after a week in office than Starmer ever achieved. The new prime minister has a net approval rating of +13, with a blitz of voter-pleasing policies appearing to have given a boost to the former mayor of Greater Manchester.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFirst EditionOur morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it mattersPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHow could Britain look under proportional representation? See the results for your areaRead moreIn addition, YouGov’slatest voting-intention pollfo the Times and Sky News showed that Labour and the Tories are now within touching distance of Reform UK. Labour appears to be enjoying a “Burnham bounce”, with the party at its most popular since January.It shows Labour just two points behind Reform – with Farage’s party on 23% of the vote, Labour on 21% and the Conservatives on 20%.YouGov gives Labour its highest figure recorded by the pollsters since January, up five points from the 16% low recorded for the party four times between March and early May this year.The polling continues to show a tightening between the three parties. In the aftermath of May’s local elections, Reform UK polled a 28% vote share, giving them an 11-point lead over any other party.In his first cabinet meeting, Burnhampromised to lead a “cost of living government”,and has used a string of early morning announcements this morning to grab the public’s attention.His first major announcement since taking office was a cut toVAT on electricity billsfrom October, beforecapping bus fares at £2and giving pubs, clubs and live music venuesa 20% discount on their business rates billsas part of a £100m aid package. Burnham has faced questions abouthow these measures will bepaid for, but the new administration insists all measures are fully funded.Explore more on these topicsReform UKNigel FaragenewsShareReuse this content

title: Water bosses’ pay rises despite bonus ban and public fury over bills and pollution | Water industry | The Guardian
description: Exclusive: Eight companies expect to be covered by the ban for 2025-26, the Guardian can reveal
Author: Jasper Jolly
Headline: Exclusive: Eight companies expect to be covered by the ban for 2025-26, the Guardian can reveal
Content: South West Water’s Countess Wear sewage treatment works in Devon. Its sewer storm overflow has spilled in the past.Photograph: Graham Hunt/AlamyView image in fullscreenSouth West Water’s Countess Wear sewage treatment works in Devon. Its sewer storm overflow has spilled in the past.Photograph: Graham Hunt/AlamyWater industryWater bosses’ pay rises despite bonus ban and public fury over bills and pollutionExclusive: Eight companies expect to be covered by the ban for 2025-26, the Guardian can revealJasper JollyFri 24 Jul 2026 13.09 EDTFirst published on Fri 24 Jul 2026 13.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWater company bosses’ total pay rose over the past year despite a government bonus ban and public outrage over pollution and bills, the Guardian can reveal.One chief executive, Mark Thurston of Anglian Water, received £1.9m – including a £500,000 “retention payment”, despite the bonus ban.The biggest package went to Louise Beardmore, chief executive of United Utilities, who received £2.5m – £1.1m more than the previous year.Overall reported pay packets rose by 1.5% to £25.3m for chief executives and chief financial officers in the year, thanks to salary rises and the use of pay loopholes, according to analysis of the 14 companies that serve most ofEnglandand Wales.Withwater bills soaringand with Britain’s biggest water company, Thames, on thebrink of insolvencyand about 23 million people covered byhosepipe bansas drought status looms, the revelation sparked criticism of companies for allegedly finding ways to pay their bosses more, despite the bonus ban being introduced in 2025.The news will add to pressure on Andy Burnham to clamp down on the industry. Burnham has said hewants to exert “more public control” over the water industry, and has suggested he could move Thames into temporary government ownership after years of financial struggles and mismanagement.View image in fullscreenMark Thurston, chief executive of Anglian Water, received £1.9m, including a £500,000 ‘retention payment’.Photograph: Geoff Moore/Rex/ShutterstockAdrian Ramsay, a Green party MP, said: “The astronomical sums paid to water company executives are a perfect illustration of everything that is wrong with treating this essential public resource as a private commodity.“Andy Burnham must surely now reach the obvious conclusion that water should be brought back into public ownership, as the Green party would do, so that any money raised goes back into the system, not into shareholders’ pockets and excessive executive pay.”Water company pay has come under intense scrutiny in recent years because of persistent dumping of sewage into Britain’s rivers and seas. The utilities have been allowed to raise bills sharply to make belated investments in their leaking pipes, ageing treatment works and new reservoirs. Recent hot weather has added to the frustrations of customers.Eight companies said they expect to be covered by the bonus ban for 2025-26, with bans applied retrospectively to companies responsible for the most serious pollution incidents or financial failings.Yet despite the ban and heavy criticism, total pay for chief executives and chief financial officers reported by water companies was £25.3m for the year to the end of March, up from £24.9m the year before, according to analysis of company accounts. It is thesecond year in a row that executive pay has risendespite the bonus ban.In some cases the companies have given their bosses extra awards that they claim are not “performance-related payments”, or bonuses, which they argue means the cash is not covered by the ban.Anglian Water said it will be caught by the bonus ban, but still gave more to Thurston. The chief executive, who was Britain’s best-paid public servant when he ran thelate and hugely over-budget HS2rail project, received the bulk of his pay through Anglian’s parent company, including a £500,000 “retention payment”.Anglian, which provides water and sewerage services to nearly 7 million customers in the East of England, claimed the payment did not count as a bonus because it was not linked to the regulated water company’s performance. The company said the payout was funded by shareholders for work outside the regulated company, and it needed “targeted, time-limited retention arrangements to maintain leadership continuity”.Yorkshire Water said it was likely to be banned from paying bonuses, but its parent company, Kelda Holdings, paid another £600,000 to its chief executive, Nicola Shaw, on top of her fixed pay of £732,000. The regular payment – which Yorkshire has said is not related to the water company’s performance – was firstrevealed last year by the Guardian.View image in fullscreenNicola Shaw received remuneration from Kelda Holdings as well as Yorkshire Water.Composite: Graham Turner; Yui MokGary Carter, a national officer for the GMB union, which represents many water workers, said: “Finding ways round the bonus ban further tarnishes the reputations of private water companies. It makes them look like money-grabbing asset strippers who care more about lining their own pockets than providing fresh, clean water for the UK public.“Senior executive pay is out of control and the government needs to fundamentally overhaul the water companies – with more public control – to fix it.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionExecutive pay dropped at some of the companies covered by the ban, including Severn Trent, Southern Water and Northumbrian Water – although Northumbrian also made a £300,000 “retention payment” to its chief executive, Heidi Mottram. However, theHigh Pay Centre, which scrutinises executive pay, said the analysis raises questions over whether the government’s bonus ban has been effective in cutting pay for those companies who are responsible for serious pollution, or which have failed financially.Andrew Speke, the High Pay Centre’s interim director, said: “These figures show the government’s current measures have not gone far enough. Restricting bonuses makes little difference if executives continue to receive broadly the same overall level of pay through other forms of remuneration. The government could go further by introducing measures such as maximum pay ratios, but more fundamentally it needs to address the corporate governance model that has allowed these levels of executive pay to persist despite years of poor performance.“If Thames Water does come under public ownership or control, ministers should seize the opportunity to demonstrate a different approach to executive pay and corporate governance. Setting clear expectations that pay should reflect performance and the public interest would establish a benchmark for the rest of the sector and increase pressure on other water companies to follow suit.”The water company reports showed other ways used by water companies and their owners to reward executives. United Utilities does not expect to be banned from paying bonuses this year, but it still gave Beardmore a £435,000 “annual allowance” with no performance conditions, on top of a 16% increase in fixed pay to £971,000. The FTSE 100 company, which has 7.3million customers, said the money came from shareholders, and was required to retain its leaders.View image in fullscreenUnited Utilities gave Louise Beardmore a £435,000 ‘annual allowance’ with no performance conditions on top of a 16% rise in fixed pay to £971,000Wessex Water was also banned from paying bonuses. However, it granted its chief executive, Ruth Jefferson, a14% salary increase. Wessex said the higher salary better reflected the job’s responsibilities.The other companies that indicated they would be covered by the ban were Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water and Thames. Thames stillpaid £4.1m in bonuses to senior staffnot covered by the ban.The water regulator for England andWales, Ofwat, is not expected to confirm formally which companies are subject to the bonus ban until the autumn. However, the ban applies retrospectively to any company responsible for the most serious pollution incidents during that year, as well as those such as Thames Water which are failing financially.A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs said: “We have banned undeserved bonuses for water company bosses. Any attempt to circumvent the rules is completely unacceptable.“We will leave no stone unturned in ensuring bonuses can only be paid where companies deliver environmental and customer outcomes and Ofwat’s review of the bonus rule will carefully consider if any requirements need to be tightened.”Water UK, which represents companies across country, declined to comment.The Guardian’s analysis included pay awarded to all people who held chief executive or chief financial officer roles during the respective years, including from parent companies where reported. Two companies did not disclose pay for chief financial officers.Explore more on these topicsWater industryExecutive pay and bonusesWaterEnglandWalesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Singer D4vd had impregnated teenager he is accused of fatally stabbing | Los Angeles | The Guardian
description: Celeste Rivas Hernandez, who was 13 at the time, later received an abortion, text messages indicate
Author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
Headline: Celeste Rivas Hernandez, who was 13 at the time, later received an abortion, text messages indicate
Content: A picture of Celeste Rivas Hernandez at a press conference following the arrest of David Anthony Burke in Los Angeles, California, on 20 April 2026.Photograph: Daniel Cole/ReutersView image in fullscreenA picture of Celeste Rivas Hernandez at a press conference following the arrest of David Anthony Burke in Los Angeles, California, on 20 April 2026.Photograph: Daniel Cole/ReutersLos AngelesSinger D4vd had impregnated teenager he is accused of fatally stabbingCeleste Rivas Hernandez, who was 13 at the time, later received an abortion, text messages indicateUwa Ede-OsifoFri 24 Jul 2026 19.25 EDTFirst published on Fri 24 Jul 2026 16.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSinger D4vd had impregnated the teenager he is accused of fatally stabbing, according to evidence presented in aLos Angelescourtroom on Friday. Celeste Rivas Hernandez later received an abortion, text messages between the two indicate.The musician, who was born David Anthony Burke, apologized to Rivas Hernandez in January 2024 for “putting her through this”, in a text message obtained from his phone.“Neither of us are capable of watching and taking care of the baby. it’s for the best no?” Rivas Hernandez replied. She was 13 years old at the time.The revelation came on the fourth day of a hearing to determine whether the musician will stand trial for murder and child sexual abuse charges linked to Rivas Hernandez’s death. He has pleaded not guilty.Speculation swirled online over whether Rivas Hernandez had been pregnant after prosecutors previewed their plan to present text correspondence with references to pregnancy, abortion and a Plan B emergency contraceptive in an April court filing.Prosecutors say Burke fatally stabbed Rivas Hernandez, who was 14, in April 2025 to silence her from divulging the sexual nature of their relationship as his career soared. He was 18 and she was 13 when the sexual abuse began, according to prosecutors.The abortion appeared to have weighed heavily on Rivas Hernandez.“I care abt u i killed my kid [for] you,” she wrote in an August 2024 text to Burke, theLos Angeles Times reported. “i don’t like talking about it cause it gets [me really] upset but id do anything to have it back.”Rivas Hernandez’s parents left the room as Corey Farell, a Los Angeles police detective, discussed explicit photographs the pair took of each other naked, Courthouse Newsreported.Beth Silverman, the deputy district attorney, apologized to Rivas Hernandez’s mother, Mercedes Martinez. “It’s too much,” she said.In February 2024, Burke suggested to police officers he believed that Rivas Hernandez was 18, according to a video presented to court earlier in the week. Law enforcement had been investigating a missing person’s report.In text messages, shown on Friday, Burke seemed to reference past encounters with authorities.“I can’t wait to move in tg without the cops bitching baby,” he wrote to Rivas Hernandez in June 2024, according to Courthouse News.He also floated the prospect of the two eloping in Italy.The autopsy of Rivas Hernandez’s body was also discussed on Friday.Last September, Los Angeles police discovered Rivas Hernandez’s remains in the front trunk of a Tesla, registered to Burke, five months after prosecutors allege Burke killed her.The court has seen graphic photographs of Rivas Hernandez’s dismembered and decomposing body this week.The degraded conditions of her remains posed challenges to the autopsy, Grant Ho, the doctor who performed the postmortem examination, testified on Friday.Rivas Hernandez had been dead for weeks when her body was found, but Ho noted it was “extremely difficult to tell” when exactly she died.In April, Rivas Hernandez’s autopsy report was unsealed amid mounting scrutiny and speculation over the circumstances of her death. According to the Los Angeles county medical examiner’s office, she died from multiple penetrating injuries.On Friday, Ho said he had identified two stab wounds – one on her abdomen that struck her liver and another on her left chest that damaged her ribs.Defense attorney Marilyn Bednarski appeared to call into question the extent to which the autopsy report could reveal what preceded Rivas Hernandez’s death.“You can’t rule out that she was holding an instrument that caused either of those wounds?” she asked Ho.The doctor said he could not, but noted that self-inflicted injuries typically are paired with “hesitation marks” on the skin, which the teenager’s remains did not have.The Associated Press contributed reportingExplore more on these topicsLos AngelesUS crimeCaliforniaWest CoastnewsShareReuse this content

Morris/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesTrump administrationTrump administration admits canceling clean energy grants to Democratic statesCourt fillings show grants denied to states if they didn’t back Trump’s re-election, but administration claims it’s a ‘misrepresentation’US politics live – latest updatesLucy CampbellFri 24 Jul 2026 17.26 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 17.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheTrump administrationhas admitted scrapping more than $7.5bn in federal grants for clean energy projects to states “based solely” on whether they backedDonald Trumpin the 2024 election.US federal officials appeared to acknowledge incourt documentslast week that they had terminated the funding last October “based solely” on political criteria, targeting projects in states that were represented byDemocratsand had voted forKamala Harris.The administration previouslyframedthe move as safeguarding taxpayer dollars from “waste” and continues to insist it was not politically motivated.Two dozen states sue Trump White House for politicizing Fema disaster aidRead more“[The Department of Energy] accepts that neither the inclusion of the ARCHES grant nor any other grants in the October notice tranche was based on any programmatic, statutory, cost-reduction or performance-based factor,” government lawyers said in the filing.“[The Department of Energy] accepts that the inclusion of grants in the October notice tranche was based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state, ie, whether the recipient’s location and/or place of performance was in a Blue State or a non-Blue State.“[The Department of Energy] will not contend that it looked beyond the prime grantee(s) to consider the political identity or geographic distribution of downstream beneficiaries of the grant funds.”The apparent admission was first reportedby the New York Times.In a statement on Friday, a spokesperson for the US energy department said of the report: “That is a misrepresentation of the court filing. None of the termination decisions were based on political considerations.”The acknowledgment of political considerations “was referring to the timing of the announcement, not of the decisions themselves”, the spokesperson claimed.The filings stem from alawsuit, filed last June, by a group of six University of California faculty and other researchers challenging various federal agencies that halted Biden-era funding.The plaintiffs said in a press release at the time that the abrupt cancellations of already-awarded grants had been a part of a “political ‘cost-cutting’ agenda and ideological purity campaign” waged by the administration.It comes as the White House seeks to exert even greater control over billions of dollars in annual federal grants, aiming to have Trump’s political appointees review all federal grants, with the power to block or revoke vast amounts of funding if they did not conform to or align with Trump’s priorities.According to a400-pageproposed rule for federal financial assistance published on 29 May, “Discretionary awards must, where applicable, demonstrably advance the President’s policy priorities.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Around 2-3 times a daySign up toBreaking News USGet the most important news as it breaksPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThey must also adhere to further standards set out by the White House, including not promoting “anti-American values”, the denial of “the sex binary in humans” and the use of “racial preferences” in selection criterion.Per last week’scourt filing, the energy department had reviewed its financial assistance awards and created a list last September that recommended canceling more than 600 grants awarded by the Biden administration for a wide range of clean energy projects in states represented by both Republicans and Democrats.However, in October, the White House budget office, led by Russell Vought, terminated only 284 of those grants. Voughtannouncedon X: “Nearly $8 billion in Green New Scam funding to fuel the Left’s climate agenda is being canceled. The projects are in the following states: CA, CO, CT, DE, HI, IL, MD, MA, MN, NH, NJ, NM, NY, OR, VT, WA.”Last week, federal officials appeared to concede that the decision had been purely informed by politics. “With one exception, the 284 terminated grants had a recipient location and/or at least one place of performance in a state that awarded its electoral votes to Kamala Harris in the 2024 election and has two Democratic-caucusing Senators (“Blue State” grants),” the court filing says.Meanwhile, the energy department left in place hundreds of other energy grants in state represented by Republicans and that had voted for Trump in 2024 – despite the department having also recommended that they too be scrapped.Last month, Trump’s energy secretary, Chris Wright, appeared before the House science, space and technology committee to defend his department’s fiscal 2027 budget request. “No decisions were made on politics,” he insisted.The Guardian has reached out to the White House.Explore more on these topicsTrump administrationUS elections 2024Donald TrumpDemocratsUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Pogacar conquers Alpe d’Huez in record climb to win stage 19 and extend Tour de France lead | Tour de France 2026 | The Guardian
description: Tadej Pogacar conquered the famed hairpins of the Alpe d’Huez in a record time as he won stage 19 of the Tour de France to extend his overall lead
Author: Jeremy Whittle
Headline: Tadej Pogacar conquered the famed hairpins of the Alpe d’Huez in a record time as he won stage 19 of the Tour de France to extend his overall lead
Content: Slovenia's Tadej Pogacar looks to the sky after his incredible stage win on Alpe d’Huez.Photograph: Thibault Camus/Pool AP/APView image in fullscreenSlovenia's Tadej Pogacar looks to the sky after his incredible stage win on Alpe d’Huez.Photograph: Thibault Camus/Pool AP/APTour de France 2026Pogacar conquers Alpe d’Huez in record climb to win stage 19 and extend Tour de France leadSlovenian only second man to win in yellow on mountainLeader opens up gap of more than seven minutesJeremy Whittlein Alpe d'HuezFri 24 Jul 2026 12.25 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 19.19 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTadej Pogacar put further distance between himself and his last remaining rivals, winning the Alpe d’Huez stage of theTour de Franceand extending his overall lead to more than seven minutes.There was a brutal inevitability about the defending Tour champion’s win on the legendary climb of the Alpe, despite all the rumours of illness and gastric problems within his UAE Emirates XRG team.Pogacar’s climbing time, of 35 minutes and 26 seconds, shattered the longstanding record set by Marco Pantani in 1997, by more than a minute.“I don’t know what the time of Pantani was,” he said. “I don’t take too much into that, but I heard that I broke the record, so I’m happy.“I would say this means as much as any other win, but now everyone has emphasised how big this win is, maybe I will start to realise it is quite important.“I just wanted to do a good race and to win. A thirtysomething year record finally broken is good for us.”So feverish was the speculation over Pogacar switching from yellow shorts to black earlier this week, that one French TV commentator even suggested it was to conceal an excess of flatulence. But on the Alpe, it didn’t matter what colour Pogacar’s shorts were: he still won.View image in fullscreenTadej Pogacar chases down the lead breakaway group on the Alpe d’Huez ascent.Photograph: Anne-Christine Poujoulat/AFP/Getty ImagesThe only wind emanating from the four-time Tour winner, now close to taking a record-equalling fifth win in Paris on Sunday, came from the metronomic climbing style that took him to a record-breaking ascent of the Alpe’s 21 hairpin bends.The Slovene looked the picture of health as he sped up the 13.8 kilometre climb, the theatre for many of the Tour’s most dramatic finishes, and with one final mountain stage still to come, now seems assured of overall victory in Paris.The old adage, that the Tour is won on the Alpe, was proven again with Pogacar’s latest demolition of his hapless rivals. With 25km left to race, the day’s breakaway led by almost four minutes, but three kilometres from the finish, Pogacar had caught and overtaken them.Pogacar’s sports director, Matxin Fernández, was reduced to tears by his rider’s performance. “I don’t know why they get so emotional,” Pogacar said of his team management. “I don’t cry often. I guess it meant a lot to the team and also the way we are riding as a team, the team spirit we have. It cannot be better, so when we win, the emotions come to the surface.”Huge and rowdy crowds, estimated to be in the region of 500,000, and at times out of control, greeted the riders at the foot of the Alpe. Some had arrived six days in advance, while others seemed too intoxicated to know why they were there in the first place.“It was a crazy atmosphere on the climb,” Pogacar said.The damage done to his rivals was extensive, with Remco Evenepoel the least wounded by the onslaught. The Belgian remains in second place overall, but any hopes of challenging for the final victory are long gone. He and Pogacar’s teammate, Isaac del Toro, are now the only riders within 10 minutes of the race leader.View image in fullscreenTadej Pogacar fights through the throng on stage 19.Photograph: Dario Belingheri/Getty ImagesOn another day of desperation for the teams that have yet to taste success in this year’s Tour, a big breakaway took shape on the early climbs of the Bayard and Noyer.In that leading group of 40 were some now familiar names, including past stage winners, Richard Carapaz, Thymen Arensman, winner of two stages in 2025, and the recovering Adam Yates, teammate to Pogacar, who won in Bilbao in 2023.It was a Lazarus-like performance from Yates, who was so sick earlier this week that he was barely able to pedal through the finish line to his team bus after Wednesday’s stage to Voiron. But as soon as the main contenders began to climb the first steep ramps of the Alpe, the stage took on a new look, as Pogacar shifted up a gear.His decisive acceleration came 12km from the summit and immediately left his closest rivals in his wake. After joining forces with Yates, the pair ate into the break’s advantage, until with 10km remaining, Pogacar set off alone.The denouement was obvious. It was a cruel and relentless win, wholly in character with Pogacar’s domination of the Tour. He has taken five wins in 19 stages. Saturday’s “queen” stage, over four of the hardest climbs in the Alps, now offers him the chance to take a sixth. Another victory now seems almost inevitable.Explore more on these topicsTour de France 2026Tour de FranceCyclingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Austin FC academy players under investigation by police and FBI for allegations of youth-on-youth sexual abuse | Austin FC | The Guardian
description: Multiple league, club, and law enforcement sources confirm ongoing inquiries into MLS club
Author: Alexander Abnos
Headline: Multiple league, club, and law enforcement sources confirm ongoing inquiries into MLS club
Content: Austin FC began play in Major League Soccer in 2021.Photograph: Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAustin FC began play in Major League Soccer in 2021.Photograph: Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesAustin FCAustin FC academy players under investigation by police and FBI for allegations of youth-on-youth sexual abuseAustin FC reported allegations to local law enforcementMultiple sources confirm the ongoing inquiriesAlexander AbnosandPablo Iglesias MaurerFri 24 Jul 2026 17.45 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 18.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMultiple players in the academy of Major League Soccer clubAustin FCare under investigation by Austin police and the FBI over allegations of sexual abuse within the club’s youth system. Multiple sources, who spoke to the Guardian on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the investigation, said the inquiry centers on alleged interactions between academy players. A source with knowledge of the matter said multiple academy families reported the allegations to Austin FC.The Austin police department confirmed the existence of the investigation to the Guardian on Thursday, adding that because it “involves juveniles and is ongoing”, no other details could be shared. An FBI spokesperson said the bureau could “neither confirm nor deny” the existence of an investigation and declined to comment further. Sources atMLSand Austin FC confirmed the existence of the Austin police department and the FBI’s investigations.“In December 2025, we became aware of allegations of youth-on-youth misconduct occurring among a group of academy players,” the Austin FC Academy said in a statement issued to the Guardian. “After learning of these issues from concerned Academy families, Austin FC Academy took immediate action.”The academy said in its statement that its officials immediately reported the allegations to MLS, the US Center for SafeSport and local law enforcement and initiated an internal investigation in coordination with the league. The academy also suspended “all activities” for the age group affected by the allegations while the issues were investigated. The FBI has visited the club’s training facility to conduct interviews, a club source told the Guardian.Sources within MLS and Austin FC said that multiple academy players had been disciplined as a result of their investigation but that no Austin FC academy staff member had been. That same source said the league and club could pursue additional action if new information arises, but both Austin FC and the league itself have been asked to pause their own proceedings until law enforcement concludes theirs.“We continue to fully cooperate with law enforcement throughout its ongoing investigation,” the Austin FC Academy said in a statement to the Guardian. “Throughout this process, Austin FC Academy and MLS took decisive actions guided by our unwavering commitment to the health, safety and well-being of our youth players and will continue to do so.”“MLS takes matters of player safety and well-being extremely seriously,” the league said in a statement to the Guardian. “Throughout the process, MLS and Austin FC have approached this matter from a trauma-informed perspective, prioritizing the safety and well-being of the young people involved, protecting their privacy, minimizing the risk of further harm, and coordinating carefully with law enforcement and other appropriate authorities. MLS prioritizes the safety and well-being of players and will continue to work with clubs to promote a safe and respectful environment.”The Austin FC academy program comprises five teams, from U-13 to U-18 age groups. At least 100 players are involved in the program, which is overseen by a separate coaching staff and leadership structurefrom the senior team. The teams compete in MLS Next, the youth competition run by the league that started in 2020. Like many MLS academies, Austin FC recruits from around the country and offers homestay living arrangements for players arriving from out of town. They also provide schooling for their players via an agreement with Florida-based SAI academy, who provide on-site education for many MLS academies.At the senior level, Austin’s sporting department has changed significantly in recent months, with the club moving on from head coach Nico Estévez and sporting director Rodolfo Borrell in May. On Friday, a club source said those changes were not connected to the allegations. Austin eventually installed former Philadelphia Union head coach Jim Curtin as Estevez’s replacement, though he will not take charge until the start of the 2027 sprint season. The team, led by interim head coach Davy Arnaud, sit 14th out of 15 teams in the Western Conference, three points clear of last-place Sporting Kansas City.Explore more on these topicsAustin FCMLSUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: CBS analyst Tony Romo arrested on suspicion of DUI in Wisconsin | NFL | The Guardian
description: The former Cowboys quarterback performed poorly on field sobriety tests and was arrested on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The former Cowboys quarterback performed poorly on field sobriety tests and was arrested on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence
Content: Tony Romo has been a lead analyst for CBS since 2017.Photograph: Michael Ainsworth/APView image in fullscreenTony Romo has been a lead analyst for CBS since 2017.Photograph: Michael Ainsworth/APNFLCBS analyst Tony Romo arrested on suspicion of DUI in WisconsinRomo booked for operating vehicle under the influenceFirst-offense OWI is not criminal charge in WisconsinAssociated PressFri 24 Jul 2026 15.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTony Romo, the CBSNFLanalyst and former Dallas Cowboys quarterback, has been arrested on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence.According to an arrest report by the Milwaukee county sheriff’s office, Romo performed poorly on field sobriety tests after getting stopped while driving south on Interstate 43 on Thursday. Sheriff’s officials said Romo was taken into custody, booked and released.Romo went to high school about 35 miles from Milwaukee in Burlington, Wisconsin. He was in town to golf in the annual Wisconsin Amateur Championship, perWisconsin Public Radio.In Wisconsin, a first-offense OWI is not a criminal charge. It typically carries a $150 to $300 fine. Romo has a court appearance set for 21 September.The 46-year-old Romo has been the lead game analyst for CBS’s NFL coverage since 2017 after making four Pro Bowl appearances during an NFL career that ran from 2004 to 2016 and was spent entirely with Dallas.CBS had no comment regarding the arrest.Romo remains the Cowboys’ franchise leader in career touchdown passes with 248. He held the franchise record for career passing yards (34,183) until Dak Prescott overtook him last season.Explore more on these topicsNFLUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: LeBron James set to sign with Philadelphia 76ers in NBA free agency blockbuster | LeBron James | The Guardian
description: The 41-year-old is set to join Philadelphia on a reported two-year, $8m deal with a player option after spending the last eight seasons with the Lakers
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: The 41-year-old is set to join Philadelphia on a reported two-year, $8m deal with a player option after spending the last eight seasons with the Lakers
Content: LeBron James is headed to Philadelphia.Photograph: Jae C Hong/APView image in fullscreenLeBron James is headed to Philadelphia.Photograph: Jae C Hong/APLeBron JamesLeBron James set to sign with Philadelphia 76ers in NBA free agency blockbusterStar will play record 24th NBA season in PhillyDeal is reportedly two years, $8m with player option41-year-old spent last eight seasons with LakersAnalysis: LeBron to Philly is perfectly in characterGuardian sportFri 24 Jul 2026 11.44 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 14.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLeBron James is signing with thePhiladelphia 76erson a two-year, $8m deal that includes a player option. Klutch Sports Group CEO Rich Paul confirmed the terms of the agreement to ESPN, and James addressed the move in a post on X on Friday morning, saying it came after he strongly considered retirement.“I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time,” he said.The move pairs the NBA’s all-time leading scorer with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and the newly acquired Jaylen Brown as Philadelphia bolster their roster in pursuit of a first NBA championship since 1983. James arrives after spending the past eight seasons with theLos Angeles Lakers.LeBron James going to the Philadelphia 76ers is perfectly in characterRead moreThe deal gives James the flexibility to become a free agent again after one season while limiting the 76ers’ long-term financial commitment. James made nearly $53m with the Lakers last season.The 41-year-old wrote in his X post that he believed he was “done” and had played the final game of his storiedNBAcareer before deciding to sign with Philadelphia for a record 24th season.“I wasn’t ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game,” James rote. “I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and deicide if I still love this game. I still truly love this game, and I have more to give.“The last few weeks have really been special. I’ve never been able to have no clue what to do and take real time to just think. I’ve had an incredible few months with all the people I love trying to figure it all out. This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship.”The 76ers went 45-37 last season and were swept in the second round of the playoffs by the eventual champion New York Knicks. They have been active this offseason, acquiring Brown, a five-time All-Star and the 2024 Finals MVP, earlier this month via trade. They have not advanced past the second round of the playoffs since 2001.View image in fullscreenJaylen Brown and LeBron James, pictured in a 2018 game between the Celtics and the Cavaliers, will be teammates in Philadelphia.Photograph: Cj Gunther/EPAJames is a four-time NBA champion, four-time MVP and the league’s all-time leading scorer. He is the NBA’s oldest active player and averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists for the Lakers last season. His announcement at the end of June that he would not return to the Lakers led to much speculation about his next destination, with Golden State, Cleveland and Miami – he led the latter two teams to championships – allfloatedas potential landing spots.The signing will become official once it is completed under NBA rules.“Thank you LA. Miami I’ll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always home!” James said in his post.Explore more on these topicsLeBron JamesNBABasketballUS sportsPhiladelphia 76ersLos Angeles LakersnewsShareReuse this content

title: Lando Norris hits out at Formula One for putting money ahead of drivers | Lando Norris | The Guardian
description: Many drivers are unhappy with the new regulations and Lando Norris, the reigning world champion, said: ‘F1’s gone too heavily led by the fact it’s a business’
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Many drivers are unhappy with the new regulations and Lando Norris, the reigning world champion, said: ‘F1’s gone too heavily led by the fact it’s a business’
Content: Lando Norris has spoken out about his frustrations this season.Photograph: Boglárka Bodnár/EPAView image in fullscreenLando Norris has spoken out about his frustrations this season.Photograph: Boglárka Bodnár/EPALando NorrisLando Norris hits out at Formula One for putting money ahead of driversMany drivers also unhappy with new regulations‘F1’s gone too heavily led by the fact it’s a business’Giles Richardsat the HunagroringFri 24 Jul 2026 12.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 12.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLando Norris has delivered a scathing critique of Formula One and its management for prioritising making money over sporting considerations when forming the sport’s new regulations. The world champion argued that the drivers should have been more involved in the process.Norris is amongmany drivers who have been clear this seasonhe is unhappy with the new regulations, their focus on energy management and how it has affected negatively their enjoyment of driving. It is a problem he believes had been created because F1 framed the rules in order to attract new engine manufacturers into the sport.‘Eyes forward now’: George Russell upbeat after Mercedes solve engine problemRead more“The thing that’s a shame is that Formula One’s gone too heavily led by the fact it’s a business nowadays and not how can you make the sport the best possible,” he said. “It’s how can you just make the most money as a business and that’s just not what it should simply be. That’s not how a sport should be run.”The use of an almost 50-50 split in electrical power and the internal combustion engine is understood to have been central in attracting manufacturers such as Audi and Honda into F1 this season. However, it has proved hugely unpopular with drivers, who now have to manage their use of energy rather than being able to race flat out and has introduced some variables into performance influenced by the algorithm that governs the deployment of electrical power.Norris believes drivers’ complaints were being listened to but they did not carry great weight against the financial imperative he felt was driving the sport.“They listen but you can’t just change your engine in the middle of the year and you can’t change it even with one or two years’ notice because it’s not about making the best performance of a car … it’s a business,” he said. “Everyone wants to make money, so in order for Audi and other teams to come in we had to change these things. It’s a shame, it should never have been like that. But that’s how businesses work.“The biggest voice should always be ours as drivers and that’s not because we’re selfish in saying that but because we have the best idea of how racing should be, how it can be, what’s possible, what’s not. We would just want the best for everything and at the minute, we don’t.“We have very, very little say and a lot more of it’s done because if you can have Audi and other teams in it, it’s a bigger win than the drivers being happy.”The shortcomings of the new regulations were shown starkly at the last two rounds at Silverstone and Spa. Both circuits are considered energy-starved, leading to a chorus of complaints over race weekends, and at Spa the lack of power left one of the great tracks an anodyne affair.View image in fullscreenMax Verstappen was second in Friday’s first practice.Photograph: Marco Canoniero/ShutterstockAt the Hungaroring this weekend there will at least be some respite from the issue, with the preponderance of corners ensuring plentiful recharging and that the race to be run at full pace in what will likely be a tightly contested fight.The Mercedes engine advantage will not be so pronounced on the tightly twisting circuit, where Ferrari and Red Bull will expect strong form, with Ferrari’s pace out of the corners a major boon in the last race before the summer break.In first practice, Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc topped the timesheets from the Red Bull of Max Verstappen with Lewis Hamilton in third. In the second session Hamilton was on top with Leclerc in second and McLaren’s Lando Norris third. Antonelli was in 13th place and his Mercedes teammate George Russell in fifth.Explore more on these topicsLando NorrisFormula One 2026Formula OneMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Ted Williams, Satchel Paige and the fight to induct Negro Leaguers into baseball’s Hall of Fame | Baseball | The Guardian
description: Sixty years ago, the famed Red Sox slugger used his Cooperstown speech to champion Black players who were excluded because of the sport’s color barrier
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Sixty years ago, the famed Red Sox slugger used his Cooperstown speech to champion Black players who were excluded because of the sport’s color barrier
Content: Ted Williams, the Boston Red Sox legend and the last player to hit .400 in a season, was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame on 25 July 1966.Photograph: James Drake/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTed Williams, the Boston Red Sox legend and the last player to hit .400 in a season, was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame on 25 July 1966.Photograph: James Drake/Getty ImagesBaseballTed Williams, Satchel Paige and the fight to induct Negro Leaguers into baseball’s Hall of FameSixty years ago, the famed Red Sox slugger used his Cooperstown speech to champion Black players who were excluded because of the sport’s color barrierFrederic J FrommerFri 24 Jul 2026 06.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhen Ted Williams, the last man to hit .400, was inducted into the NationalBaseballHall of Fame, he had an iconic career to reflect on. But he decided to dedicate a portion of his speech to championing Black players who had been excluded because of baseball’s longtime color barrier.“I’ve always been a very lucky guy to have worn a baseball uniform, to have struck out or to hit a tape-measure home run,” Williams said in his25 July 1966 speech– 60 years ago Saturday. “And I hope that someday the names of Satchel Paige and Josh Gibson in some way could be added as a symbol of the great Negro players that are not here only because they were not given a chance.”Williams’s plea helped build support to admit Negro League players into the Hall five years later, starting with Paige. Today, there are37 former Negro League playersin the Hall.‘Like pulling a tractor trailer’: what it’s like to play on an awful MLB teamRead more“That was a political speech,” Ben Bradlee Jr, Williams’s biographer,told Axios in 2024. “And Williams was so influential as a player, and this … had a huge effect.”The famed Red Sox slugger was inducted alongside manager Casey Stengel, in front of acrowd of 10,000 peoplein Cooperstown, New York. Wearing a suit sans tie, Williams delivered a speech he said he had written the night before in his hotel room.It came less than 20 years after Jackie Robinson had broken baseball’s color barrier with the Brooklyn Dodgers, and a year after President Lyndon Johnson signed into law the landmarkVoting Rights Act of 1965.Williams was no liberal. He was ahuge fan of Richard Nixon, especially when Williams became manager of the Washington Senators in 1969, coinciding with Nixon’s first year as president.“If You Don’t Like Policemen,” read a bumper sticker on Williams’s car, “Call A Hippie.” Senators broadcaster Shelby Whitfield, a friend of Williams, once described him as an “ultraconservative in the tradition of Barry Goldwater and John Wayne”.But Williams, who had a Mexican American mother, had a progressive attitude toward Black players, dating back to his career. When the Red Sox in 1959 finally signed their first African American player, Elijah Jerry “Pumpsie” Green – becoming the last team in the majors to do so – Williams was one of the first players to greet him,Green told journalist Steve Buckley in 1996.In 1971, MLB finally came up with aplan to admit Negro League playersto the Hall of Fame. However, it was a convoluted PR disaster, calling for the admittance of one Negro League player per year “as part of a new exhibit commemorating the contributions of the Negro Leagues to baseball”. The justification for this separate treatment was that Negro League players didn’t have the required 10 years of MLB service to qualify.View image in fullscreenSatchel Paige was inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1971.Photograph: Matty Zimmerman/APCritics slammed the approach. Paige said, “I was just as good as the white boys. I ain’t going in the back door to the Hall of Fame.” Robinson urged him to boycott that summer’s induction ceremony.“It’s not worth a hill of beans,” said Robinson, who had been inducted as the first Black Hall of Famer in 1962. “It’s the same thing all over again.”In his autobiography, Commissioner Bowie Kuhn wrote that some in theMLBestablishment didn’t want Negro Leagues players to be admitted at all – not even in a separate wing.“I found unpersuasive and unimpressive the argument that the Hall of Fame would be ‘watered down’ if men who had not played in the majors were admitted,” he wrote. “‘The rules are clear,’ said my opponents. ‘You need 10 years of major league experience. Moreover, where are the statistics to support them? There was only sketchy and sloppy record keeping in the Negro Leagues.’”“I thought these arguments were much too technical under the circumstances,” Kuhn recalled. “Through no fault of their own, the Black players had been barred from the majors until 1947. Had they not been barred, there would have been great major-league players, and certainly Hall of Famers, among them.”But when Kuhn tried to go around the opponents with a plan for a separate Negro Leagues exhibit, he wrote, “A predictable furor ensued. Cries of ‘Jim Crow’ were heard. … I was placed under personal attack for putting forth the idea.”Los Angeles Times columnist Jim Murray made that very point.“The notion of Jim Crow in Baseball’s Heaven is appalling,’’ he wrote. “What is this – 1840? Either let him in the front of the Hall – or move the damn thing to Mississippi.”Trump loomed over baseball’s Hall of Fame. But voters still said no to Bonds and ClemensRead moreMLB was forced to reverse course, and in August 1971 Paige was inducted as a regular member – the first player selected by the Committee on Negro Baseball Leagues. Although Paige played for several seasons in the American League – making his debut in 1948 at the age of 42 – he was inducted primarily because of his outstanding Negro League career. Between the Negro Leagues and the AL,he finished with a 132-82 record and a 2.83 ERA. Six white players and a former executive were inducted with him.“I am the proudest man on the Earth today, and my wife and sister and sister‐in‐law and my son all feel the same,”Paige said. “It’s a wonderful day and one man who appreciates it is Leroy ‘Satchel’ Paige.”Williams also felt gratified about his own induction speech.“One of the things that I really am kind of proud of myself about is that in my induction into the Hall of Fame, nobody encouraged me on this, I thought this thing alone,”he told Bob Costasin 1993. “And I thought, ‘I’ve seen Satchel Paige. And I’ve seen Josh Gibson. And I heard about Buck Leonard. I heard about some of the other great Black athletes.’ And it just came out that day, that I wrote in my speech, that I hope someday, that the great Black players of the past, who only because of their color, never had a chance to play in the big leagues [are inducted]. And it hit a little note.”Williams was not impressed with MLB’s original plan for a separate wing.“They come out with, I gotta say, a half-assed program for the Black players to get into the Hall of Fame,” he said. “And finally they changed that … It was a very important move.”In 1972, the year after Paige’s induction, Josh Gibson and Buck Leonard, two stars from the old Homestead Grays known as “the Black Babe Ruth” and “the Black Lou Gehrig”,were inducted into the Hall of Fame. They became the first inductees who played their entire careers in the Negro Leagues.Gibson died of a stroke at the age of 35 in 1947, so his son, Josh Gibson Jr, accepted the plaque on his behalf. But Leonard, 64, was still alive and able to relish the induction on that August afternoon.“My getting in is something I never thought would happen,” he said.Frederic J Frommer, a sports and politics historian who has written for the Washington Post, the New York Times, the Atlantic and other national publications, is working on a book on ’70s baseball.Explore more on these topicsBaseballMLBUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: All 45 Major League Soccer players at the 2026 World Cup, ranked | MLS | The Guardian
description: Lionel Messi tops our ranking of the MLS players at the World Cup, ahead of Argentina teammate Rodrigo De Paul and Canada’s Stephen Eustáquio
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Lionel Messi tops our ranking of the MLS players at the World Cup, ahead of Argentina teammate Rodrigo De Paul and Canada’s Stephen Eustáquio
Content: Argentina’s Lionel Messi (left) and Rodrigo De Paul arrive before the World Cup final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.Photograph: Charly Triballeau/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenArgentina’s Lionel Messi (left) and Rodrigo De Paul arrive before the World Cup final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.Photograph: Charly Triballeau/AFP/Getty ImagesMLSAll 45 Major League Soccer players at the 2026 World Cup, rankedFrom Lionel Messi’s final flourish to players who barely featured, we rank every MLS representative who appeared in the 2026 World CupCatalina BushFri 24 Jul 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 11.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJump to1) Lionel Messi, Argentina2) Rodrigo De Paul, Argentina3) Stephen Eustáquio, Canada4) Mbekezeli Mbokazi, South Africa5) Matías Galarza, Paraguay6) Andrés Cubas, Paraguay7) Finn Surman, New Zealand8) Sebastian Berhalter, USA9) Steven Moreira, Cape Verde10) Aiden O’Neill, Australia11) Matt Freese, USA12) James Rodríguez, Colombia13) Juan Manuel Sanabria, Uruguay14) Richie Laryea, Canada15) Tim Ream, USA16) Lucas Herrington, Australia17) Maxime Crépeau, Canada18) Son Heung-min, South Korea19) Petar Musa, Croatia20) Danley Jean Jacques, Haiti21) Carlos Harvey, Panama22) Marco Pasalic, Croatia23) Miguel Almirón, Paraguay24) Michael Boxall, New Zealand25) Jacob Shaffelburg, Canada26) Ahmed Qasem, Iraq27) Louicius Deedson, Haiti28) Mathieu Choinière, Canada29) Matt Turner, USA30) Miles Robinson, USA31) Kai Trewin, Australia32) Braian Ojeda, Paraguay33) Derrick Etienne Jr, Haiti34) Jayden Nelson, Canada35) Aníbal Godoy, Panama36) Jonathan Osorio, Canada37) Max Arfsten, USA1) Lionel Messi, ArgentinaMessi was always going to be No 1. In what was likely his lastWorld Cup, the Argentinian put together an incredible tournament, registering eight goals, four assists and the most progressive passes of any player, according to Futi. With zero defensive responsibility on his shoulders, Messi was free to do as he liked. The 39-year-old roamed the field with ease and effortlessly drew Argentina back from the brink time and time again. It was Messi who led his country to a 3-2 win against Cape Verde, Messi who assisted and then equalized against Egypt, and Messi who created both of Argentina’s late goals against England. In the final, however, Messi disappeared. Across 139 minutes including stoppage time, Messi completed just 28 of 39 passes, registered only one shot and hardly affected the game. He may have left the tournament with no personal or team accolades – a rarity for him – but Messi extended a World Cup legacy that few players have ever to come close to rivaling.2) Rodrigo De Paul, ArgentinaDe Paul started all but two of Argentina’s games on their path to the final and played 70 minutes against Spain. The Inter Miami midfielder was aggressive and good at keeping the ball; he was never going to be the star of the show, but he played his part well and helped his nation reach a second straight World Cup final.3) Stephen Eustáquio, CanadaEustáquio was one of Canada’s primary creators and most important players at the World Cup. The midfielder put in cross after cross and generated 2.76 chances as well as 0.36 expected assists (xA) per 90 minutes. His 46 total progressive passes ranked sixth among all players at the World Cup. Then, in the dying minutes of Canada’s last-32 matchup against South Africa, the 29-year-old intercepted a clearance, chested the ball down and slotted a half-volley shot into the bottom corner, securing a first World Cup knockout victory for his nation. (Eustáquio spent the four months before the World Cup on loan with Los Angeles FC, but has since returned to Porto.)4) Mbekezeli Mbokazi, South AfricaThe Chicago Fire defender and former Orlando Pirates captain entered the tournament as South Africa’s youngest player to be called up at just 20. Yet Mbokazi appeared one of the most experienced players on the field for Bafana Bafana. His performances at the World Cup were so impressive that they turned heads internationally – his transfer value according to Transfermarkt rose from $4m prior to the tournament to more than $9m after it.5) Matías Galarza, ParaguayGalarza started in all but the first of Paraguay’s World Cup matches, scoring the lone goal against Turkey and assisting Julio Enciso’s strike against Germany in the knockouts. Paraguay’s average possession across all of their games was 29%, which ranked them last among all teams in the tournament. This certainly limited Galarza’s efficacy in the attack, but the midfielder showed he could fit within that system just fine. (Galarza departed Atlanta United after a loan and returned to River Plate.)6) Andrés Cubas, ParaguayCubas played an important role for Paraguay as their destroyer in midfield, playing every possible minute across all five games. The Vancouver Whitecaps midfielder was integral to Paraguay’s defensive stability that saw them take Germany to penalties and hold France to just one goal. In the quarter-final matchup, Cubas won seven of 12 duels, logged seven tackles and three interceptions and got into a kerfuffle with Kylian Mbappé.7) Finn Surman, New ZealandSurman had a breakout first two games for New Zealand and looked like one of the All Whites’ best players, consistently saving his nation through last-ditch tackles and crucial clearances. The 22-year-old Portland Timbers center-back contributed offensively, too, scoring New Zealand’s lone goal in their 3-1 defeat to Egypt.8) Sebastian Berhalter, USABerhalter was one of Mauricio Pochettino’s preferred substitutes, making an appearance in every match the US played. In his only start, he was deployed at the No 6 position, which created major defensive issues for the US. This was more due to the dearth of defensive midfielders on Pochettino’s roster than any personal failing of Berhalter, and the Vancouver Whitecaps man (who is reportedly bound for Middlesbrough) was still able to contribute by scoring a goal and assisting another.9) Steven Moreira, Cape VerdeWhile he may not have grabbed as many headlines as Cape Verde’s other full-back, Sidny Lopes Cabral, Columbus’s Moreira was a centerpiece of the team’s backline and helped power his nation to near-glory against Spain, Uruguay and Argentina.10) Aiden O’Neill, AustraliaO’Neill played a familiar role for Australia, operating in much the same way he operates for New York City FC as a quiet, consistent, possession-oriented central midfielder. The veteran won the Superior Player of the Match award for his performance against Paraguay and followed it up with an impressive performance against Egypt.View image in fullscreenJames Rodríguez looked past his best for Colombia at the World Cup.Photograph: DeFodi Images/Getty Images11) Matt Freese, USALike Tim Ream, Freese had his tournament defined by one poor game and, ultimately, just one poor moment. The 27-year-old NYC FC keeper was otherwise impressive in goal; his passing was accurate and he made nine saves through four games.12) James Rodríguez, ColombiaRodríguez, 12 years after his breakout World Cup in Brazil, appeared aged in the United States, where he joined Minnesota United on loan earlier this year. Just two years ago, he put together a legacy run at Copa América with one goal and six assists in six matches, leading Colombia to a heartbreaking second-place finish behind Argentina. That magic that Rodríguez summoned then, and on so many previous occasions, escaped him in his final outing on the world’s stage. Moments of quality remained, but with no end-product to show for it and a disappointing last-16 exit to Switzerland, Rodríguez’s World Cup journey, like his club career, came to a drawn-out, empty close.13) Juan Manuel Sanabria, UruguaySanabria started two of Uruguay’s three group-stage games, including their final match against Spain, where the Real Salt Lake man was tasked with defending Lamine Yamal. The Spaniard was mostly quieted by Sanabria; Yamal created just 0.03 xG and 0.10 xA while only completing five of his 12 attempted dribbles.14) Richie Laryea, CanadaLaryea contributed 0.26 xA per 90 minutes during the World Cup and helped progress the ball along Canada’s left flank, but struggled at moments defensively. Against Bosnia and Herzegovina, it was Laryea’s mark that opened the scoring off of an in-swinging corner, and in the Switzerland match, Laryea was frequently out of position or unwilling to track back. The Toronto FC defender has long been a mainstay of the Canada team, but his performances in this World Cup lacked any real spark.15) Tim Ream, USAFor a second, it seemed as if the capital-V Veteran defender had hardly aged since Qatar. That notion came crashing down, alongside the rest of the US team, in a 4-1 thrashing at the hands of Belgium. Ream, however, was perhaps the game’s greatest casualty. On Belgium’s opener, the 38-year-old Charlotte center-back was caught unaware by an in-form Charles De Ketelaere, who scored a poacher’s goal with Ream nowhere to be seen. Then, just two minutes after the US equalized, Ream was humiliated by De Ketelaere yet again as the Belgian climbed above him to reach a back-post cross and slot it in the back of the net.16) Lucas Herrington, AustraliaAt just 18, Herrington ranked as the youngest player on Australia’s World Cup roster but nevertheless, the Colorado Rapids center-back worked his way into the squad, earning a start in each of Australia’s final two matches.17) Maxime Crépeau, CanadaCrépeau, who plays for Orlando City, left the tournament with six goals conceded and a meager six saves through five games.18) Son Heung-min, South KoreaThe World Cup was full of disappointment for the 34-year-old. Son was unable to score in either of his two starts, and the LAFC forward was left on the bench in South Korea’s must-win final group-stage game.19) Petar Musa, CroatiaThe FC Dallas striker, through two starts and 110 minutes for Croatia, managed just one shot, which he converted.20) Danley Jean Jacques, HaitiPhiladelphia’s Jean Jacques operated alongside Jean-Ricner Bellegarde in Haiti’s double pivot, but given Haiti’s status as the lowest-ranked team in the tournament, the midfield pair faced an uphill battle in every match.21) Carlos Harvey, PanamaHarvey started in all three of Panama’s group-stage games and apart from a couple of dangerous headers off of corners and throw-ins, the 6ft 1in Minnesota midfielder had a mostly quiet tournament.22) Marco Pasalic, CroatiaThe 25-year-old Orlando City winger managed a productive start in Croatia’s third group-stage game but made a mess of his one golden opportunity to get on the scoresheet.View image in fullscreenSon Heung-min reacts at the end of South Korea’s World Cup group-stage match against South Africa in Monterrey, Mexico.Photograph: Moisés Castillo/AP23) Miguel Almirón, ParaguayAlmirón registered just four shots and 0.11 xG through four World Cup starts, but the Atlanta attacker will almost exclusively be remembered for receiving a red card against Turkey after covering his mouth during an “altercation” between the two teams. It was the first example of the International Football Association Board’s new mouth-covering ban being implemented.24) Michael Boxall, New ZealandThe veteran Minnesota defender came into the tournament as one of its oldest players, and appeared a half-step behind on nearly every goal that the All Whites conceded.25) Jacob Shaffelburg, CanadaLAFC’s Shaffelburg appeared as a substitute in all five of Canada’s matches, but was unable to meaningfully affect the game when on the field.26) Ahmed Qasem, IraqQasem appeared in all of Iraq’s games and played a full 90 minutes against France. The Nashville forward started again in the final group-stage match but was hooked early amid a tactical reshuffle after the ejection of Iraq’s Rebin Sulaka in the 13th minute.27) Louicius Deedson, HaitiFC Dallas winger Deedson played in all three of Haiti’s group-stage losses, totaling 112 minutes and 13 completed passes.28) Mathieu Choinière, CanadaThe LAFC midfielder made just one appearance: a start in Canada’s 2-1 loss to Switzerland.29) Matt Turner, USAThe former starting goalkeeper for the US and current New England Revolution No 1 was handed the start against Turkey and conceded three goals while registering not a single save.30) Miles Robinson, USAIt became clear throughout the World Cup that Pochettino had little faith in his defensive backups, with the FC Cincinnati center-back’s only minutes coming in a meaningless final group-stage game.31) Kai Trewin, AustraliaThe NYC FC defender replaced the injured Jordan Bos at half-time of Australia’s knockout match against Egypt and helped see the game to penalties.32) Braian Ojeda, ParaguayThe Orlando City midfielder’s only cameo was a 21-minute outing against Germany in the last 32, during which he logged just nine touches.33) Derrick Etienne Jr, HaitiThe Toronto winger played nine minutes against Brazil in Haiti’s second group-stage match, completing four passes.34) Jayden Nelson, CanadaThe Austin FC winger entered in the 87th minute of Canada’s knockout matchup against Morocco that finished in a 3-0 loss.35) Aníbal Godoy, PanamaGodoy completed eight of eight passes in his single minute plus stoppage time against Ghana, but the San Diego midfielder was unable to prevent the opponent from scoring a last-minute winner in the dying seconds of the match.36) Jonathan Osorio, CanadaToronto’s captain made two substitute appearances in the 87th minute or later, with neither outing being particularly fruitful.37) Max Arfsten, USAThe Columbus winger entered at the 90th minute of the US’s 4-1 round of 16 loss to Belgium and was unable to touch the ball before the final whistle.Did not playChris Brady, USA (Chicago)CJ dos Santos, Cape Verde (San Diego)Rayan Elloumi, Tunisia (Vancouver)Herman Johansson, Sweden (Dallas)Olwethu Makhanya, South Africa (Philadelphia)Cristian Roldan, USA (Seattle)Dayne St Clair, Canada (Miami)Joel Waterman, Canada (Chicago)Explore more on
