title: Tyson Fury defeats 46-year-old Mariusz Wach in warm-up for expected Joshua bout | Tyson Fury | The Guardian
description: Tyson Fury fulfilled his side of the bargain for a potential heavyweight blockbuster against Anthony Joshua by stopping veteran Polish fighter Mariusz Wach in Pattaya, Thailand
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Tyson Fury fulfilled his side of the bargain for a potential heavyweight blockbuster against Anthony Joshua by stopping veteran Polish fighter Mariusz Wach in Pattaya, Thailand
Content: Tyson Fury overwhelmed the 46-year-old Mariusz Wach.Photograph: Athit Perawongmetha/ReutersView image in fullscreenTyson Fury overwhelmed the 46-year-old Mariusz Wach.Photograph: Athit Perawongmetha/ReutersTyson FuryTyson Fury defeats 46-year-old Mariusz Wach in warm-up for expected Joshua boutFight in Pattaya, Thailand had no live broadcastAnthony Joshua faces Kristian Prenga on SaturdayPA MediaFri 24 Jul 2026 13.41 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 14.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTyson Fury fulfilled his side of the bargain for a potential heavyweight blockbuster againstAnthony Joshuaby stopping the veteran Polish fighter Mariusz Wach in Pattaya, Thailand.About 1,500 fans watched the bout, which had no live broadcast, and saw Fury largely dominate his overmatched 46-year-old opponent, who slipped to an eighth defeat in his past 11 contests. While Wach remained upright, he was pulled out after the end of the seventh round by his corner, battered into submission by Fury, who made it back-to-back wins in 2026 after a 16-month layoff.Fury and Joshua shadow-box their way towards overdue $100m showdownRead moreAll eyes will now turn to Joshua’s fight against unheralded Albanian Kristian Prenga in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia on Saturday night – although Fury said he is not planning to be in attendance. If Joshua is victorious then it should pave the way for a long-awaited and much-anticipated “Battle of Britain” against Fury.After Joshua announced he would return to the ring against Prenga – his first fight since being involved in a car crash in December in Nigeria that killed two of his closest friends – Fury also decided on a tune-up, havingoutpointed Russia’s Arslanbek Makhmudovin April.For only the fourth time in 39 fights and the first in 15 years, Fury was leaner than his opponent after clocking 265lb, nearly two stone lighter than Wach, who was 291.4lb at Thursday’s weigh-in. The 6ft 9in Fury had the height and reach advantages, though, and used his jab to control the range, as well as switching between orthodox and southpaw stances to confuse his rival.While Wach is a former world title challenger,losing to Wladimir Klitschko in 2012, he is a fading force and was stopped inside two rounds by rising British prospect Moses Itauma two years ago. Wach found the target with the odd right hand but Fury was the busier and more punishing fighter, at one point landing five uppercuts in a row to the cheers of a partisan crowd.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFury, who has based his training camps in Thailand sincereversing his retirementat the start of the year, beat Makhmudov in front of 60,000 fans at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium but was undeterred by fighting in front of a smaller crowd. Following the end of the seventh round, the contest was waved off by the referee after Wach’s corner indicated their charge was unable to continue as Fury improved his record to 36-2-1, with 25 knockouts.Explore more on these topicsTyson FuryAnthony JoshuaBoxingnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Two holes and I’m there for the Claret Jug’: DeChambeau says two-shot penalty cost him Open | Bryson DeChambeau | The Guardian
description: Bryson DeChambeau believes he would have been ‘right there for the Claret Jug’ if he had not received a two-shot penalty in the Open Championship
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Bryson DeChambeau believes he would have been ‘right there for the Claret Jug’ if he had not received a two-shot penalty in the Open Championship
Content: Bryson DeChambeau at the LIV Golf event in Uttoxeter.Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenBryson DeChambeau at the LIV Golf event in Uttoxeter.Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty ImagesBryson DeChambeau‘Two holes and I’m there for the Claret Jug’: DeChambeau says two-shot penalty cost him OpenGolfer punished for flattening grass around shotAmerican threatened to pull out of tournamentPA MediaFri 24 Jul 2026 05.30 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 05.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBryson DeChambeau believes he would have been “right there for the Claret Jug” if he had not receiveda two-shot penalty in the Open Championshiplast week at Royal Birkdale.DeChambeau made a positive start to last week’s tournament after opening with a 67 and then a 66 on Friday, but his second-round score was later adjusted to 68 after he was handed a retrospective two-stroke penalty at the 5th hole after a video review. The 32-year-old was punished after match officials ruled he had improved the area of his backswing by standing on and flattening some long grass.DeChambeau moves the dial for golf but is his posturing and pantomime worth the hassle? | Ewan MurrayRead moreDeChambeau was in the mix at the top of the leaderboard but he dropped from second to fifth in the standings after his bogey was subsequently turned into a triple bogey. The American protested against the decision and even threatened to pull out of the tournament, but he played through the weekend and made 69 in the third round before a final-day 72.Ryan Fox clinched victory to claim his first ever major championship at 10 under and DeChambeau finished six shots back at four under, but he feels the two-shot penalty played a pivotal role in his weekend.DeChambeau is now playing in LIVGolfUK at the JCB Golf and Country Club near Uttoxeter and he said there: “Yeah, I made the cut. It was a good fight. I wish I’d have given it more on Saturday and Sunday, it felt like I could have.“Besides the 5th, being three over on it, and the 11th, that’s six shots. That’s tied for the lead right there. Two holes and I’m right there for the Claret Jug.”After missing the cut in his previous three major championships, DeChambeau’s tied 14th place finish gave him his strongest performance in a major since he was runner-up to Scottie Scheffler at the 2025 US PGA Championship.Explore more on these topicsBryson DeChambeauGolfThe OpenEuropean TourPGA TourUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘You need to evolve’: Enzo Maresca plots life after Pep at Manchester City | Enzo Maresca | The Guardian
description: The Italian does not shy away from the task of following a legend in Pep Guardiola but his previous time at the club may help him
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: The Italian does not shy away from the task of following a legend in Pep Guardiola but his previous time at the club may help him
Content: ‘I’m confident we can do a great job,’ Enzo Maresca said as he returned to Manchester City to replace Pep Guardiola.Photograph: Manchester City FCView image in fullscreen‘I’m confident we can do a great job,’ Enzo Maresca said as he returned to Manchester City to replace Pep Guardiola.Photograph: Manchester City FCEnzo Maresca‘You need to evolve’: Enzo Maresca plots life after Pep at Manchester CityItalian does not shy away from the task of following a legend but his previous time at the club may help himJamie JacksonFri 24 Jul 2026 14.13 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 16.22 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRelaxed and tanned, Enzo Maresca offered a warm note with his first words to the media as the manager ofManchester City, who must somehow follow the generational Pep Guardiola. “Before we start, I would like to send a message and a big hug to Kevin Keegan’s family for this moment,” said the Italian in tribute to a football legend, following his death on Monday.Keegan, of course, was a former City manager who had at Newcastle famously locked horns with Sir Alex Ferguson when he led Manchester United, the fierce rivals of Maresca’s new team. When the 46-year-old, sat on the dais occupied for 10 mostly glittering years by Guardiola, offered an unsolicited reference to Ferguson – and Arsène Wenger – you could see he comprehended the mammoth task before him.Elliot Anderson lauds City as ‘kings of Manchester’ after £116m Forest transferRead moreHow do you follow the man who claimed 20 trophies in a decade and who ranks alongside Ferguson? Well, by mentioning, and so trying to tame, the elephant in the room. “The history of the manager with many years in the same club always struggled a little bit. After Sir Alex, after Arsène,” Maresca said. “But also, it’s a challenge to try to do the right things immediately for this organisation, for the fans, for everyone.”Speaking in front of a giant “Welcome back Enzo” billboard, a reference to his previous leading of City’s elite development squad in 2020-21 as well as his stint as Guardiola’s assistant manager in the 2022-23 treble season, Maresca would have been aware the font of goodwill will not prove deep if results go south. Certainly not from that most fickle of constituencies – fans. So Maresca cutely pointed to the patience of City’s chairman, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, and his executive. “This club has had three managers in 17 years,” he said. “This is not normal, so this is one of the things that I’m confident we can do a great job and continue to do the job that has been done in the last years. Roberto [Mancini] was here, then Manuel [Pellegrini] and then Pep – for 10 years.”View image in fullscreenEnzo Maresca with Pep Guardiola at a June 2023 Manchester City training session.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPAMancini’s tenure began in December 2009, ended with his sacking in May 2013, and was angst-ridden: anathema to al-Mubarak and his chief executive, Ferran Soriano. If Mancini could be volatile, Pellegrini proved serene, and Guardiola was, simply, a genius. Al-Mubarak’s and Soriano’s experience of Maresca during his two previous seasons at City obviously convinced them that he is the full package: an accomplished football man who is of equable character.Yet Maresca’s exit from his previous post at Chelsea on New Year’s Day ended with an apology from him, and City paying the west London club £17m in compensation. Maresca’s shutters came down for the first – and only – time when his conduct was raised. “I feel quite lucky in terms of my former clubs – Leicester, Chelsea – I think we did a great job,” he said. “In both clubs, the identity of the team was clear, the success of the team was clear, and I feel very lucky to be part of these clubs. But now we are here today. That is the most important thing, just about City. And nothing to add.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMaresca says managing Manchester City ‘a privilege’ but admits challenge of following GuardiolaRead moreMaresca made Leicester Championship champions and the next season took Chelsea to fourth in the Premier League and a Conference League triumph before claiming the Fifa Club World Cup last summer, a 3-0 evisceration of Paris Saint-Germain in the final a calling card that may well have sealed the City job.He talked of “titles” for the coming season. To aid this mission, Maresca has Elliot Anderson, a £116m buy from Nottingham Forest, to patrol midfield, and potentially Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, who shone for Morocco at the World Cup, to further bolster this department. He also retains an interest in Malo Gusto, one of his right-backs when at Chelsea, and if Omar Marmoush leaves, the market will be entered for a similar, pacy forward.One player Maresca certainly does not wish to lose is the peerless Rodri, who lifted the World Cup for Spain on Sunday and received the Golden Ball, and whose control of a contest in the ever-more frantic domestic game is priceless. The 30-year-old will have surgery on a back problem on Monday. The word is it is not too serious, though he will miss out when City host Bournemouth on the opening weekend of the season. The more important date is 1 September, when the transfer window closes: will Real Madrid have made a move for a footballer who has a year left on his terms and is declining to sign the new deal offered by City?Of more immediate concern for Maresca is flying out on Tuesday for a pre‑season tour of Asia that features matches with Inter in Hong Kong and K-League All Stars and Atlético Madrid in Seoul. For the trip Maresca will have back City’s A-listers who exited the World Cup early, including Josko Gvardiol, Mateo Kovacic and Abdukodir Khusanov.View image in fullscreenElliot Anderson was a key player for England at the World Cup and was Manchester City’s first signing of the summer.Photograph: Marta Lavandier/AP“I’m working at the moment with many young players,” he said. “That is always good because they are full of energy and some of them are very good. The last group of players are going to join three or four days before the Community Shield and we will have all the squad.” After that Cardiff game with Arsenal on Sunday 16 August, the bid to successfully succeed Guardiola begins in earnest.“You need to adapt, evolve,” Maresca added in reference to his playing style. “Set pieces, man to man – it’s a little bit the direction where football is going. We managers, it’s our duty to find solutions.” We are about to discover how good he is at this.Explore more on these topicsEnzo MarescaManchester CityFootball tacticsPep GuardiolafeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Jürgen Klopp vows to change Germany but threatens to quit if family hounded by media | Jürgen Klopp | The Guardian
description: Jürgen Klopp was optimistic after being confirmed as Germany’s new head coach but warned the media to ‘leave my family in peace’
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: Jürgen Klopp was optimistic after being confirmed as Germany’s new head coach but warned the media to ‘leave my family in peace’
Content: Jürgen Klopp talks to the media at his presentation as Germany’s new head coach.Photograph: Markus Ulmer/GES Sportfoto/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJürgen Klopp talks to the media at his presentation as Germany’s new head coach.Photograph: Markus Ulmer/GES Sportfoto/Getty ImagesJürgen KloppJürgen Klopp vows to change Germany but threatens to quit if family hounded by mediaSuggests role will be his final job in top-level footballWarns journalists to ‘leave my family in peace’Nick AmesFri 24 Jul 2026 08.08 EDTFirst published on Fri 24 Jul 2026 05.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJürgen Klopp said he wants his team to “change a country” after being confirmed as Germany’s new head coach, but threatened to stand down if his family are hounded by the media during his time in charge.In a forthright first press conference upon his unveiling as Julian Nagelsmann’s replacement, Klopp also suggested the role will be his final job in top-level football and expressed regret after poking fun at his predecessor while working as a television pundit during the World Cup. He is tasked with reviving Germany, who lost to Paraguay in the last 32 and have not made the last 16 sincewinning the tournament in 2014.It marks a return to the dugout for Klopptwo years after leaving Liverpool, where he ended a glorious nine-season tenure after explaining he felt fatigued. Since January 2025 he hasworked as head of global soccerfor Red Bull but a comeback to frontline action had appeared inevitable sinceNagelsmann departed on 3 July.View image in fullscreenJürgen Klopp was in forthright mood in his first press conference as Germany head coach.Photograph: Hannes Albert/EPAKlopp vowed to transform a deeply fractured relationship between the national team and Germany’s public, citing his work at Liverpool as an example of the way football can galvanise a wider community.“I want to create a situation where fans go home after the game and say: ‘Wow, that was cool,’” he said. “I want people to say: ‘Wow, it was worth putting the TV on for 90 minutes to see Germany play.’ I’ve lived and experienced how football can change a city. And I think it’s not only about cities, it’s also about the country. Ideally, football can change a country.”The 59-year-old’s contract will run until after the 2030 World Cup. Klopp, however, warned that he would not tolerate invasive treatment from journalists and that he would be prepared to depart without compensation if he felt his family’s privacy had been violated.“I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you treated Nagelsmann,” he said. “I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you’ve treated, in England, Thomas Tuchel. The day you don’t want me any more, I’m gone, without any severance pay. If you say tomorrow: ‘He’s shit,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away.“Criticise me if something doesn’t work. Jürgen Klopp is not going to have any career after the national team. This is the pinnacle of my career as a coach. I will give it everything I’ve got.”Klopp was criticised last month when, speaking with the former Germany player Thomas Müller on television during coverage of the group stage match with Curaçao, he appeared to hint Nagelsmann’s days were numbered by saying he was “still” picking the team. That was followed by a quick apology; Klopp repeated the sentiment on Friday and said the pair have yet to speak since his appointment was confirmed.View image in fullscreenJürgen Klopp, in his role as Magenta TV pundit, with Kylian Mbappé after France’s World Cup quarter-final against Morocco.Photograph: Greg M Cooper/EPA“We haven’t had any exchange,” he said, wishing Nagelsmann a happy 39th birthday for Thursday. “It was a joke. In retrospect it was one of the worst ‘funny’ remarks I have ever made. I feel awfully sorry, I’ve apologised a million times.“It was just a rash thing to say, with no ulterior motive whatsoever, and I can only wish him the best.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Now he can go on to pastures new and I’m absolutely sure he will have many opportunities to coach a big team in future.”Klopp promised Germany will play expansive football with wingers but admitted they must find their own way to compete with the depth of talent available elsewhere. “Success is performance relative to expectations,” he said. “When we ask in Germany: ‘Are we as good as France?’ and the answer is no, that’s not true. If we ask: ‘Do we have players like Dembélé, Mbappé, Doué and Barcola?’, no we don’t, but we can still beat them.Germany are no longer a tournament team and must reconnect with our own identity | Philipp LahmRead more“We don’t want to play like Argentina, Spain, England or France. We want to do it the German way, very intense. Are we the No 1 team right now? No, we accept that. There are 11 teams ahead of us in the ranking. We can beat them, but for this to happen we need to play very good, very intense football.”International football will demand a change of rhythm for Klopp after a lifetime spent in the domestic game. “I think contact with a team is not necessarily about working with them day in, day out,” he said. “Sometimes it will be 30 minutes or an hour and that will be on the pitch. But all of them have a mobile. I’ll talk to them, listen to them, watch games and give my feedback. That, too, is developing players and making them better.”Klopp’s reign will begin with a ­baptism of fire in Amsterdam against the Netherlands on 24 September, one of four Nations League games in the space of 11 days. “The players have to show me, and not just say it, that playing for Germany is a super special thing,” he said.Explore more on these topicsJürgen KloppGermanynewsShareReuse this content

title: Dismissed solicitor is still acting for footballers in brain injury court case | Concussion in sport | The Guardian
description: Richard Boardman, the solicitor dismissed by rugby players suing the game’s authorities over brain injuries, continues to lead a similar claim by footballers
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Richard Boardman, the solicitor dismissed by rugby players suing the game’s authorities over brain injuries, continues to lead a similar claim by footballers
Content: Richard Boardman addressed a hearing at the Royal Courts of Justice this week.Photograph: Aaron Chown/PAView image in fullscreenRichard Boardman addressed a hearing at the Royal Courts of Justice this week.Photograph: Aaron Chown/PAConcussion in sportDismissed solicitor is still acting for footballers in brain injury court caseRichard Boardman dropped by group of rugby playersFootball group includes family of Nobby StilesMatt HughesFri 24 Jul 2026 15.39 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 16.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe solicitor dismissed by a group of over 1,000 rugby players with brain injuries who are suing the sport’s governing bodies is still leading a similar claim on behalf of dozens of former footballers.Richard Boardman told a hearing at the Royal Courts of Justice this week of his intention to “come off the record,” with the claimants indicating that they had unanimously agreed to terminate their dealings with his firm, Rylands Garth.Rugby brain injury case reaches crisis point as judge retires to consider 95% strikeoutsRead moreBoardman’s management of the case was strongly criticised by the presiding judge, Master Jeremy Cook, who highlighted alleged “widespread non-compliance” and “misleading evidence,” with particular regard to his failure to make good on a pledge to provide the court with all of the claimants’ medical records.Master Cook is now considering whether to strike off the case entirely, which would leave a large cohort of former union and league players including England World Cup winners Steve Thompson and Phil Vickery with nothing to show for six years of gruelling legal battles.Despite being dismissed by the rugby players however, Boardman is still acting on behalf of a group of 23 former footballers who are suing the Football Association, English Football League and FA of Wales as a result of permanent brain injuries sustained during their careers.The group includes the families of World Cup hero Nobby Stiles, former Newcastle manager Joe Kinnear and four former players from the Premier League era. With a far smaller number of claimants, and as a result fewer medical records, the football case is seen as more manageable for Rylands Garth.Coincidentally, the FA changed their defence team in the case earlier this year and both parties remain in the process of exchanging documents.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe rugby claimants are in the process of appointing new solicitors, but until they have done so Boardman remains notionally in charge despite being absent from court for the last day and a half of hearings this week. The firm Leigh Day has been consulting on the case since February and is considering whether to take it on.Explore more on these topicsConcussion in sportRugby unionRugby leaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Andoni Iraola backs backroom staff to help cure Liverpool’s set-piece ills | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Andoni Iraola has outlined the roles his backroom staff will play in trying to improve Liverpool’s set-piece record next season
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Andoni Iraola has outlined the roles his backroom staff will play in trying to improve Liverpool’s set-piece record next season
Content: Andoni Iraola will take charge of Liverpool for the first time in a pre-season friendly against Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAView image in fullscreenAndoni Iraola will take charge of Liverpool for the first time in a pre-season friendly against Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PALiverpoolAndoni Iraola backs backroom staff to help cure Liverpool’s set-piece illsTommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper to work on set-piecesIraola felt ‘very lucky’ to work with them at BournemouthAndy Hunterin ChicagoFri 24 Jul 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 16.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAndoni Iraola has outlined the roles his backroom staff will play in trying to improve Liverpool’s set-piece record next season and admitted he was “very lucky” to inherit a talented coaching team at Bournemouth.Iraola has brought several members of his Bournemouth backroom team with him to Liverpool sincesucceeding Arne Slot last month. Tommy Elphick, a boyhood Liverpool fan, and Shaun Cooper have joined as first-team coaches while Iraola’s long-time colleague Pablo de la Torre has arrived as assistant coach. Alejandro Rosalen has taken over as first-team goalkeeping coach after five years with Napoli.‘Don’t become the protagonist’: Andoni Iraola on the secret of Spain’s success and his role at LiverpoolRead moreIraola worked alongside De la Torre in his first coaching job at AEK Larnaca, and again at Rayo Vallecano, and said having trusted confidants alongside him would be invaluable for his first season in charge at Anfield. “For me, it was important they came with me,” said Iraola, who will take charge of his firstLiverpoolgame on Saturday in a pre-season friendly against Sunderland in Nashville. “Pablo is a physical coach but has been with me almost all the years I have been coaching. So, for me, he is much more than a physical coach really. He is an assistant and we know each other very well.“I was very lucky with Tommy and Shaun when I arrived at Bournemouth. Because I was unlucky to have the issue with my assistant coach Iñigo Pérez [who was denied a work permit when attempting to follow Iraola from Rayo Vallecano to Bournemouth]. After, it worked out very well for him because now he is coaching Villarreal. Maybe we play him in the Champions League.“But when I had Tommy and Shaun there, we did not feel the need to bring in another assistant. They were very prepared, they were very helpful for me in terms of understanding the English culture, the mentality of the players, what they were used to, what they like in training, even the small details that maybe in Spain are different. Also the experience Tommy has at Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Huddersfield; they can be in a closer position to the players. They can feel more identified. I am a little bit older. Some of the players maybe didn’t know I was a player.”One requirement for Iraola and his backroom staff will be to address Liverpool’s problems at set pieces. Only Bournemouth (26), Crystal Palace (25) and Leeds (24) conceded more set-piece goals than Liverpool’s 23 in what proved Slot’s final season as head coach, having won the title in his first. “They are very good coaches,” said Iraola. “We kind of ­understand the game similarly and they have different roles in the coaching staff, they help with set pieces also. That’s the reason I continued with them.“Tommy does defensive set plays, Shaun does more offensive, more ­creative ones. But also we are working very well here with the set-piece analyst [Lewis Mahoney], who was very good in the second half of last season. He is already with the club, so they are working on some stuff.”Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolAndoni IraolanewsShareReuse this content

title: Transfer news: Newcastle sign Monaco’s Bamba, Summerville joins Al-Hilal | Newcastle United | The Guardian
description: Newcastle have made Aladji Bamba their fourth signing of the summer after the 20-year-old midfielder completed a move from Monaco
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: Newcastle have made Aladji Bamba their fourth signing of the summer after the 20-year-old midfielder completed a move from Monaco
Content: Aladji Bamba said he ‘can’t wait to be on the pitch’ after signing for Newcastle.Photograph: Courtesy of Newcastle UnitedView image in fullscreenAladji Bamba said he ‘can’t wait to be on the pitch’ after signing for Newcastle.Photograph: Courtesy of Newcastle UnitedNewcastle UnitedTransfer news: Newcastle sign Monaco’s Bamba, Summerville joins Al-HilalMidfielder agrees five-year contract after £34m moveDutch winger leaves West Ham in deal worth £60mLouise Taylorand agenciesFri 24 Jul 2026 16.10 EDTFirst published on Fri 24 Jul 2026 06.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNewcastle have made Aladji Bamba their fourth signing of the summer after the 20-year-old midfielder ­completed a move fromMonacofor a fee that could rise to £34m.“I’m very happy to be here,” said Bamba. “I was very excited when I heard Newcastle were interested in signing me. I know about the ­history of the club and I’ve visited the ­stadium, which is amazing. I can’t wait to be on the pitch.”Men’s transfer window summer 2026: all deals from Europe’s top five leaguesRead moreBamba, who has agreed a five-year contract, is Newcastle’s fourth signing this summer aged 20 or under. The France youth midfielder – who made 25 appearances for Monaco last season, impressing in Ligue 1 and the Champions League – joins the ­former Reims goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (20), the former Hoffenheim winger Bazoumana Touré (also 20) and the former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur (18). As a natural No 6, Bamba will be expected to compete with Lewis Miley for the midfield anchor role vacated whenSandro Tonali joined Tottenhamfor an initial £92.5m.Newcastle’s transfer policy is to sign players aged 24 or under ­costing, broadly, between £20m and £40m and possessing high resale potential. The idea is to help ensure a club that have recently negotiated a three-year settlement agreement with Uefa after breaching European spending rules remain on the right side of football’s squad investment regulations.“Aladji adds a range of ­qualities to our midfield with huge ­potential for growth,” said Eddie Howe, ­Newcastle’s head coach. “His ­development since breaking through at Monaco has been really ­impressive and is something we believe we can build on.”Howe hopes Bruno ­Guimarães will be at Newcastle to ease Bamba’s ­adaptation to Premier League life. The Brazil midfielder is wanted by Arsenal and appears keen to join Mikel Arteta’s team. However, the price is a stumbling block. ­Newcastle’s ­reluctance to sell their captain dictates they have let it be known through intermediaries that they will reject any offer in the region of £70m for a player who turns 29 in November.Arsenal have still to make a formal offer and whether they are prepared to go beyond £75m remains to be seen. Much may hinge on whether Guimarães returns to Newcastle from a holiday in Brazil, as planned, next week before joining his teammates at a training camp at La Manga in southern Spain.Summerville seals £60m Al-Hilal moveCrysencio Summerville has left West Ham to join the Saudi Arabian club Al Hilal, the Hammers have announced.The Netherlands winger joined West Ham from Leeds two years ago but was unable to prevent their relegation to the Championship last season. After previous links with Italian club Roma, the 24-year-old has signed a four-year contract with Al-Hilal.“West Ham United would like to thank Crysencio for his service and wish him well for the future,” the Hammers said in a statement. The club are yet to make any new signings this summer, but their transfer budget will be boosted by Summerville’s fee – an initial £55m, rising to a possible £60m with add-ons.View image in fullscreenCrysencio Summerville has left West Ham for Al-Hilal after two seasons at the club.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAHullhave signed the Japan midfielder Hidemasa Morita on a two-year deal, with a club option of a further year. The 31-year-old, who has won 40 caps for his country, joins as a free agent after leaving Portuguese club Sporting.Evertonhave confirmed the departure of midfielder Idrissa Gana Gueye, who leaves after 236 appearances in two separate spells. Gueye’s contract expired on 30 June, and talks over a potential extension have come to nothing. He is expected to sign a one-year deal with Saudi club Al-Diriyah in due course.“Everyone at Everton is hugely grateful for Gana’s dedication on the pitch throughout his two spells at the club,” said the club’s manager, David Moyes. His commitment to the club over many years was exceptional.”Explore more on these topicsNewcastle UnitedTransfer windowMonaconewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester United and the quest to make mythical midfield a reality | Soccer | The Guardian
description: In today’s Football Daily: Sensible spending at Old Trafford, and Jürgen Klopp is back with a bang
Author: Dominic Booth
Headline: In today’s Football Daily: Sensible spending at Old Trafford, and Jürgen Klopp is back with a bang
Content: Andrey Santos (right) is the latest midfielder brought in to  try to solve the Manchester United midfield puzzle.Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAndrey Santos (right) is the latest midfielder brought in to  try to solve the Manchester United midfield puzzle.Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesFootball Daily newsletterSoccerManchester United and the quest to make mythical midfield a realitySign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!Dominic BoothFri 24 Jul 2026 10.02 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 11.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMIDDLE MENLike the urban myth that you are never more than three feet away from a spider, modern footballing lore tells us Manchester United are only ever three signings away from a Premier League title challenge. With the Geopolitics World Cup in the rear-view mirror and the transfer news machine churning once more, you may have missed United being linked with just about every midfielder to ever grace a centre circle. They missed out on Elliot Anderson – who went and dubbed his new club the“kings of Manchester”– and were fooled into thinking they could snare Aurélien Tchouaméni. They danced briefly with Atalanta’s Éderson, before landing on Chelsea resale project prospect Andrey Santos and former Aston Villa linchpin Youri Tielemans. And United aren’t done with their midfield overhaul – rightly so given they have lost Casemiro to Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte to long-term knee knack. Next up on United’s extensive longlist:Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavingaand Fulham’s Sander Berge, plus France GWC sensation Manu Koné as Michael Carrick eyes the final piece in his midfield puzzle.The problem with United over the past 13 years has been that it’s never actually the final piece. It would be kind to call their post-Ferguson transfer hit rate scattergun. Ángel Di María was the first final piece in the puzzle. Then it was Alexis Sánchez. Then Fred. And then Jadon Sancho. Something needed to change. So say what you like about Big Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s recent, purse-tightening Old Trafford regime, but they’ve not flopped anywhere near as hard in the transfer market as their predecessors. Only Ugarte and Joshua Zirkzee can be deemed true flops under the Ineos boys. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha were smart additions a year ago, Senne Lammens was a scouting triumph and United are threatening to go again with their sensible signings policy – who’d have thunk it?! – with a combined £85m on Santos and Tielemans representing far better value than splashing that same amount on relegation specialist Matheus Fernandes. Finding value in the market is almost impossible nowadays, but credit to these fellas, they’re giving it a go.What feels quite apt with Carrick at the wheel is that United’s biggest struggle this summer has been to find a true midfield destroyer. That moniker certainly doesn’t fit Santos, nor Tielemans. Tchouaméni was always unattainable so United are getting creative, as they did when Carrick was sought as Roy Keane’s replacement in 2006, less a like-for-like replacement and more a style shift. OK, it could be argued that Berge – an experienced screening No 6 – could step into the Casemiro void after a promising GWC campaign, but Camavinga and Koné like to charge around putting out fires, so perhaps United are following the mould of other top clubs and dispensing with the idea of the Makélélé role.Modern football is all about excess, whether that be GWC participants, number of games, or transfer fees going beyond £100m for apparently workmanlike players. United have long threatened to descend into financial overspill, but after a steady season under a steady manager, are they finally grasping the concept of modest frugality? Roll up, roll up: ditch the merch-baiting marquee signing and grab yourself three all-purpose midfielders, all for reasonable prices! It surely cannot last.QUOTE OF THE DAY“This is ideally the high point of my career, of my life, my professional life. I will give it everything I have [but] if you [reporters] tomorrow start saying: ‘He’s sh!t,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away” – Jürgen Klopptakes the Germany joband proves that he should still be good for a quote or two.View image in fullscreenJürgen Klopp: still got it.Photograph: Markus Ulmer/GES Sportfoto/Getty ImagesFOOTBALL DAILY LETTERSdouble quotation markRe: Simon Mazier’s letter about the location of Iraola’s Amazon parcel (Thursday’s Football Daily). If the delivery guy is anything like ours, the player will turn up at the Etihad” – Dave Eddy.double quotation markIt would be even worse for Iraola to receive a card saying that his new signing has been left with a neighbour … Everton” – Paul Taverner.double quotation markAt least if Bezos buys into Liverpool, they get next-day delivery, music, and a TV channel. They can also send back any players they don’t want and get a full refund” –Jeff BezPeter Arnold.double quotation markMatt Targett is staying in the north east with Hull City (yesterday’s email edition)? The north east begins at the River Tees, some 110 miles north of Hull. Geography lessons needed” – Geoff Brodie (and 1,056 others).If you have any, please send letters tothe.boss@theguardian.com.Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Dave Eddy. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, arehere.RECOMMENDED FOLLOWINGBig Website: onBlueSpace,TikBook,Instachat, you name it.This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version,just visit this page and follow the instructions.Explore more on these topicsFootballFootball Daily newsletterfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente | Spain | The Guardian
description: Spain’s head coach, Luis De la Fuente, has hit out at the ‘intolerable, unacceptable’ behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Spain’s head coach, Luis De la Fuente, has hit out at the ‘intolerable, unacceptable’ behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final
Content: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente (right) watches action during the World Cup final.Photograph: Pamela Smith/APView image in fullscreenSpain head coach Luis de la Fuente (right) watches action during the World Cup final.Photograph: Pamela Smith/APSpainArgentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la FuenteSpain head coach hits out at ‘acts of aggression’Fifa investigation into incident yet to result in sanctionsAFPFri 24 Jul 2026 06.56 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 16.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSpain’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has hit out at the “intolerable, unacceptable” behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’sWorld Cupfinal.At the forefront were Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes, whoattacked Rodri and Eric García respectivelyat New York New Jersey Stadium as Spain’s players celebratedwinning the World Cupfor a second time in the country’s history. Paredes also confronted Spain’s Gavi.David Squires on … the notable people and big moments from World Cup 2026Read more“At the time, I didn’t realise it. title: Rampant Wigan sweep to derby win as St Helens’ Rowley sacking fails to spark change | Rugby league | The Guardian
description: St Helens began life after head coach Paul Rowley with a heavy 38-16 Super League defeat at rivals Wigan
Author: Aaron Bower
Headline: St Helens began life after head coach Paul Rowley with a heavy 38-16 Super League defeat at rivals Wigan
Content: Bevan French touches down Wigan’s first try against St Helens.Photograph: Olly Hassell/SWpix.com/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenBevan French touches down Wigan’s first try against St Helens.Photograph: Olly Hassell/SWpix.com/ShutterstockRugby leagueRampant Wigan sweep to derby win as St Helens’ Rowley sacking fails to spark changeSuper League: Wigan 38-16 St HelensSaints thrashed day after sacking head coach RowleyAaron Bowerat Brick Community StadiumFri 24 Jul 2026 17.04 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 20.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere may only be eight miles between rugby league’s two greatest rivals but in sporting terms,Wigan Warriorsand St Helens are simply worlds apart right now.The most tumultuous of weeks for the Saints ended in the way many it expected to: with a straightforward derby defeat. There was no shortage of effort, but there are bigger problems at a club that expects greatness – which is why Paul Rowley was relieved of his duties as Saints coach after nine months in charge on the eve of this game.Dismissed solicitor is still acting for footballers in brain injury court caseRead moreThe timing was perhaps a surprise; the decision, not so much. It simply didn’t work out, with the Saints regressing under Rowley to such an extent that he became their shortest-serving coach in 50 years. His successor has a huge job on his hands; not just to make the playoffs this year, but to oversee a rebuild beyond.The very fact there was some talk ofSt Helenskeeping this respectable representing a successful outcome for a club world champions just three years ago should be humiliating for all associated with their downfall. Yes, they are struggling with injuries, but their lowly league position underlines the size of the task Rowley’s successor has ahead.But that talk is for another day. Here, this was Wigan’s night – and there is perhaps no player that emphasises the gulf between these two legendary clubs quite like the man who stole the show here: the Warriors’ talismanic half-back, Bevan French.Back from a hamstring injury, French scored one try and created another four and added further weight to the argument he is Super League’s greatest-ever overseas player. It was in the balance at the break, with Saints’ players providing a response to Rowley’s sacking to trail by six at half-time.View image in fullscreenWigan’s Adam Keighran celebrates a try against St Helens.Photograph: Olly Hassell/SWpix.com/ShutterstockTries for Jacob Douglas and Jack Welsby put them ahead on two separate occasions either side of French’s try. The Australian then produced two superb assists for Zach Eckersley to put Wigan in front; they didn’t go behind again as they ran riot after the break, with the Saints’ young bench unable to keep up amid three more injuries to add to their mounting list.But tellingly, even after an ultimately comfortable win, Wigan’s coach demanded more. “There’s elements we can do better,” Matt Peet said. “It shows how far we’ve come as a group though that we could still get the win.”It was closely contested in the first half. The second was a mismatch. French teed up Oli Partington to score four minutes after the restart, before the half-back decided to let someone else make mischief for a brief moment, as Harry Smith’s kick sent Partington over for a second as the contest rapidly moved away from the Saints.Adam Keighran then claimed a kick from – who else – French before Wigan’s maestro was withdrawn to a standing ovation with 15 minutes left. Lewis Murphy scored a late consolation for the Saints but realistically, there is only one of these sides heading to Old Trafford for the Grand Final in October: and it is not the Saints.Their interim coach, Eamon O’Carroll, was right to praise the effort his side displayed post-match. England full-back Welsby’s performance offered some hope too. But the problems at this club run much deeper, and Rowley’s replacement will have watched this contest from wherever in the world he is currently based and seen a club with a transitional period ahead of them.In contrast, Wigan look equipped to go the distance again this year under Peet. They are a beacon of consistency while the winds of change will blow through the Saints at hurricane-strength force in the coming months. Two great clubs, with two very different autumns ahead.Explore more on these topicsRugby leagueWigan WarriorsSt HelensSuper LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Duncan Scott shines for Scotland again with 200m individual medley gold  | Swimming | The Guardian
description: Duncan Scott added to his trophy cabinet with gold for Scotland in the men’s 200m individual medley at the Commonwealth Games
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: Duncan Scott added to his trophy cabinet with gold for Scotland in the men’s 200m individual medley at the Commonwealth Games
Content: Duncan Scott celebrates his latest medal success for Scotland.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenDuncan Scott celebrates his latest medal success for Scotland.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianSwimmingDuncan Scott shines for Scotland again with 200m individual medley goldScott holds off Clareburt and England’s Tom Dean to winAdam Ramsay-Peaty wins 100m breaststroke semi-finalSean Ingleat Tollcross International Swimming CentreFri 24 Jul 2026 17.03 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 18.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere are generals from banana republics with fewer medals on their chests than Duncan Scott. And when the pressure was highest at a homeCommonwealth Games, the most decorated Scottish athlete of all time delivered again.On paper it looked like a stacked men’s 200m individual medley, with world and Olympic champions, including New Zealander Lewis Clareburt and England’s Tom Dean, lurking with intent. But Scott had other ideas.Lani Pallister opens Australia’s Commonwealth Games tally with 400m freestyle goldRead moreAfter a strong butterfly, the 29-year-old applied the squeeze on the backstroke and breaststroke and then delivered the coup de grace on the freestyle to take gold in 1min 56.38sec, nearly half a second clear of Clareburt, who took silver, with Dean claiming bronze.To make Scott’s victory even sweeter, he also broke the Commonwealth record. No wonder he lifted his arms up in the air and started to pound his chest like a silverback after leaving the pool. “I was a wee bit nervous before that,” he said. “Being one of the senior members of the team, the onus is kind of me. Those boys made it tough.”View image in fullscreenDuncan Scott glides through the water during the butterfly leg of the 200m individual medley final.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianScott has now won eight Olympic medals, 10 world medals and 14 at the Commonwealth Games. The way he is swimming, he is going to need a bigger medal cabinet by the end of next week.But this is just the start of a gruelling process. At the 2018 Commonwealth Games on the Gold Coast, he swam 11 races in five days and won six medals. In Birmingham in 2022 it was 12 in five and he won six more. So when asked how he would celebrate this latest gold, he said he did not know. “Probably an early night,” he eventually replied.View image in fullscreenA happy looking Duncan Scott shows off his gold medal.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianMeanwhile, Dean was happy with his individual bronze, knowing that better chances of winning gold lie ahead. “I have raced Duncan my whole adult career,” he said. “To stand next to him, to walk out with him in front of his crowd, it was something I will never forget. I am fortunate to call him a training partner as well as a friend.”Another star of these Games, Adam Ramsay-Peaty had to work to win his 100m breaststroke semi-final ahead of Jersey’s teenage sensation Filip Nowacki.Ramsay-Peaty was through halfway in a lightning quick 27.40sec but the 18-year-old Nowacki came back at him in the second half. But it was not quite enough as Ramsay-Peaty held on to win by less than half a second in 59.19. Australia’s Sam Williamson finished fastest in the other semi-final in 59.27.Asked about his thoughts on Saturday’s final, Ramsay-Peaty smiled. “I’m not going to shy away from the fact that I want to win,” Ramsay-Peaty replied. “I’m still going to be a scrapper.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenAdam Ramsay-Peaty powers through the water during his men’s 100m breaststroke semi-final.Photograph: The GuardianBut Nowacki, who is awaiting his A-Level results in maths, economics and physics, believes he can spring a surprise. “To race arguably the greatest breaststroker of all time is very special,” he said. “Can I beat him? I’m going to say yes. My training’s been progressing really well, so I’m going to give it my best and we’ll see who gets their hand on the wall first.”Elsewhere, it was a great night for Australia, who won four golds. It started on the first race of the night, as Lani Pallister pushed clear in the last 100m to beat New Zealander Erika Fairweather in the 400m freestyle in 3:59.56, with another Australian Hannah Fredericks taking bronze.Just 44 minutes later, Fredericks was back in the pool and had the energy to launch a late surge to win the 200m backstroke ahead of Scotland’s Katie Shanahan in a thriller.Two more golds followed as Australia then won the women’s and men’s 4x100m freestyle relays, with England taking silver in both races.Explore more on these topicsSwimmingCommonwealth Games 2026Commonwealth GamesnewsShareReuse this content

title: England gymnast Gabriel Langton suffers nasty fall in Commonwealth Games final | Commonwealth Games 2026 | The Guardian
description: Session was halted as medical staff attended to Gabriel Langton, who landed head-first during his high bar routine in the men’s team competition
Author: Yara El-Shaboury
Headline: Session was halted as medical staff attended to Gabriel Langton, who landed head-first during his high bar routine in the men’s team competition
Content: England’s Gabriel Langton chalks up prior to his floor routine on day one.Photograph: Naomi Baker/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEngland’s Gabriel Langton chalks up prior to his floor routine on day one.Photograph: Naomi Baker/Getty ImagesCommonwealth Games 2026England gymnast Gabriel Langton suffers nasty fall in Commonwealth Games finalTeenager lands head-first during high bar routineCanada win men’s team gold, with England secondYara El-Shabouryat Glasgow International ArenaFri 24 Jul 2026 16.53 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 19.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEngland’s bid for a fourth successiveCommonwealth Gamesmen’s artistic gymnastics team title ended with silver after a dramatic final overshadowed by an injury to the teenager Gabriel Langton, who was taken from the arena on a stretcher after a heavy fall from the high bar.The 19-year-old fell head and neck first on to the mat during the final rotation of the team final, bringing competition to a halt as medical staff rushed to his aid. The arena fell silent while Langton received treatment, with fellow gymnasts watching on in visible concern.Commonwealth Games 2026: Canada win men’s gymnastics team final marred by fall – liveRead moreAfter initially lying motionless, Langton responded to medical staff, moving his legs and later his hands. A dozen medical personnel carefully stabilised the England gymnast before lifting him on to a stretcher about 11 minutes after the fall. He was applauded by the crowd as he was taken from the competition floor.The incident came with England locked in a battle with Canada for the team title. At the time of the stoppage, Canada led the standings, narrowly ahead of England, while Australia occupied the bronze-medal position. Scotland remained within touching distance in fourth, with Cyprus fifth and Wales sixth.After Langton’s fall and the lengthy delay, Luke Whitehouse faced the daunting task of competing on the same apparatus immediately after his teammate’s accident. Despite a composed routine under difficult circumstances, he lost his balance on the dismount and finished on the mat, visibly disappointed as he walked away.“When something like that happens, you’ve just got to forget about it and reset,” Whitehouse said on performing after his teammate’s fall. “I just had to focus on my routine one skill at a time.“Gymnastics is such a dangerous sport and things like this remind us of that. It’s one of those things you have to put out of your mind. From what we’ve heard [Langton] is doing OK.”England finished with 238.250, leaving Canada needing 36.450 points from their final three floor routines to secure gold. The Canadians held their nerve with the veteran René Cournoyer opening with 13.500 before Félix Dolci, one of the standout performers of the day, followed with 13.700 to effectively seal the title. Canada finished on 241.400 to claim their first Commonwealth men’s team gold since 2006, upgrading the silver medals they won in 2018 and 2022.England took silver on 238.250, while Australia secured bronze with 235.650 after holding off a stirring late challenge from Scotland, who finished fourth on 234.300. Cyprus placed fifth on 228.350, with Wales sixth on 227.000.Whitehouse, expected to spearhead England’s title defence, made an excellent start by posting an impressive 14.400 on floor exercise. However, halfway through the contest England found themselves fourth behind Canada, Australia and Cyprus after three rotations, with the Canadians leading on 122.200 points.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionEngland steadily clawed their way back into contention as Australia encountered problems on the high bar. Alexander Yolshin-Cash played a key role in the resurgence, producing the best parallel bars score of the evening with a 14.100.Canada’s grip on gold briefly looked vulnerable when the experienced Cournoyer came off the high bar and scored 11.550, allowing England to close the gap. However, Dolci immediately steadied Canadian nerves with the apparatus’ highest score of the night, 14.250, to preserve their slender advantage heading into the final rotation.England responded admirably after Whitehouse’s slight stumble, with Yolshin-Cash producing another confident high bar routine. His score of 13.250 ranked fifth on the apparatus, secured qualification for the individual final and added valuable points to England’s overall total.Scotland also mounted a late push for bronze. Cameron Lynn thrilled the home crowd with a near-flawless high bar routine worth 13.500 before Hamish Carter added 12.350 after sticking his landing. Reuben Ward then scored 13.150, leaving Connor Sullivan needing something special in the final routine. Despite another excellent performance, Scotland fell just 1.350 points short as Australia’s consistency on pommel horse proved decisive.Explore more on these topicsCommonwealth Games 2026GymnasticsCommonwealth GamesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Lani Pallister puts years of setbacks behind her to spark Australia gold rush | Commonwealth Games 2026 | The Guardian
description: Australian wins 400m freestyle before Forrester pulls off 200m backstroke shock, and women’s and men’s 4x100 freestyle teams cap dominant day one
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Australian wins 400m freestyle before Forrester pulls off 200m backstroke shock, and women’s and men’s 4x100 freestyle teams cap dominant day one
Content: Lani Pallister and Jenna Forrester celebrate their gold and bronze medals in the 400m freestyle as Australia dominate day one at the Commonwealth Games.Photograph: Dean Lewins/AAPView image in fullscreenLani Pallister and Jenna Forrester celebrate their gold and bronze medals in the 400m freestyle as Australia dominate day one at the Commonwealth Games.Photograph: Dean Lewins/AAPCommonwealth Games 2026Lani Pallister puts years of setbacks behind her to spark Australia gold rushAustralian wins 400m freestyle, Forrester stuns in 200m backstrokeWomen’s and men’s 4x100 freestyle relay teams cap dominant day oneAustralian Associated PressFri 24 Jul 2026 15.26 EDTLast modified on Fri 24 Jul 2026 20.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLani Pallister has consigned years of struggle and setbacks to history, opening Australia’s medal tally at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games with the first of six gold medals in the pool. Pallister’s dominant win in the 400m freestyle – the first final on the Games swimming program – was the perfect start to a Glasgow campaign that is expected to reap her arich medal haul.Mollie O’Callaghan later spearheaded a comfortable win in the women’s 4x100 freestyle relay, while the men’s 4x100 freestyle team rounded out the session by ruthlessly capturing Australia’s sixth gold medal. Kyle Chalmers closed clinically to ensure Australia smashed their Games record from Birmingham 2022, winning in 3:09.49.Australia swimmers banned from thanking Gina Rinehart for Commonwealth Games medal bonusesRead moreBut there was nothing predictable about Jenna Forrester’s shock gold medal in the 200m backstroke. Forrester claimed bronze in the 400m freestyle, stood on the podium alongside Pallister then had to quickly prepare for her next final.Fifth at halfway and still fourth at the start of the last lap, Forrester stormed home. Forrester finished fourth in the event at the June trials and was only brought in when backstroke queen Kaylee McKeown had to pull out with glandular fever.Like Pallister, it is Forrester’s firstCommonwealth Gamesgold medal.View image in fullscreenJenna Forrester celebrates winning the women’s 200m backstroke final at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.Photograph: Mickael Chavet/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockPallister was the only 400m finalist to go under four minutes, clocking 3:59.56 to easily beat New Zealander Erika Fairweather. The 24-year-old led from the start and kicked clear late, finishing well ahead of Fairweather (4:02.65) and Forrester (4:05.25).Pallister, the daughter of three-time Commonwealth Games medallist Janelle Elford, was outside the Games record of 3:58.06, set by Australian great Ariarne Titmus in Birmingham. It was also notably short of her 3:58.87 personal best, with Pallister admitting she wasn’t happy with the time.But it represented a breakthrough win givenCovid-19 cruelled her Paris Olympicscampaign. Pallister qualified for the three distance freestyle events, but could only race in the 800m. The god-daughter of Australian sporting great Dawn Fraser also had a succession of health problems in 2021, including heart surgery and an eating disorder.“Without all the ups and downs I wouldn’t be the person or the athlete that I am today, and I think that’s really special,” she said after the win. “I’m proud of the journey that I’ve been on and I wouldn’t change it for the world.“I think it’s really shaped me into a good human.”Pallister revealed her mother is on a plane back to Australia after working at an altitude training in Sierra Nevada with the national open water swim team. “It’s amazing. I’m so fortunate that my mum has taken me the whole way through and kind of shown me the ropes, and Dawn as well,” she said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every daySign up toAustralia SportGet a daily roundup of the latest sports news, features and comment from our Australian sports deskPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionPallister is also favourite to win the 800m and 1500m freestyle, and will also contest the 200m freestyle and the 4x200m freestyle relay. “The first event of the Games is always one to set the tone, so I’m happy that I can do that for the whole team,” she said.Commonwealth Games 2026: Canada win men’s gymnastics team final marred by fall – as it happenedRead morePara swimmer Jenna Jones claimed Australia’s second gold, taking out the S13 100m freestyle on Saturday morning (AEST), before Forrester’s big upset.“I did not expect that to happen tonight - I am so over the moon,” Forrester said. “I didn’t really have much expectation going into the 400 free or the 200 backstroke, so I’m really happy with how that went.”Australian William Petric qualified fastest in the 200m medley, but was fourth in the final as Scottish legendDuncan Scott had the crowd roaringwith the host nation’s first gold.Alex Perkins was the fastest semi-finalist in the 50m butterfly, while fellow Australians Sam Williamson and Zac Stubblety-Cook reached their day-two 100m breaststroke final.Explore more on these topicsCommonwealth Games 2026Commonwealth GamesSwimmingAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content
